A worker harness performs held-out tasks. An outer agent investigates earlier harness source and traces, then modifies one or two declared surfaces—initially a planner prompt and context policy. External evaluation determines whether the successor is admitted.

The outer agent is injected as a user-owned callable. CI uses a deterministic fixture-backed SDK client; an opt-in maintainer driver may call a real SDK through the same boundary. The first authorized live run is captured once, sanitized, and retained with ties, regressions, and failures intact. Evaluation, equal budgets, mutation authority, and promotion stay outside the wrapper. See the boundary decision.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• HarnessArtifact manifest containing component references and declared interfaces.
  • Typed parameters for initial mutable surfaces such as TextParam and PolicyParam.
  • Explicit MutationSurface separating candidate-controlled components from hidden evaluation, secrets, permissions, budgets, audit history, and promotion policy.
  • Harness materialization, execution, capture, and validation.
  • Held-out task split and promotion rule.
  • Harness-specific comparison views over quality, cost, and failure behavior.
  • examples/research/harness_evolution/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• A candidate can modify only manifest-declared mutable surfaces.
  • Component references and the composite harness both retain content identity and causal lineage.
  • Harness evaluation runs fresh executions rather than trusting self-reported improvements.
  • Failed or invalid harnesses remain inspectable experience.
  • Later agents can compare complete harness code and traces, not only summary feedback.
  • Additional mutation surfaces can be registered without changing the coordinator.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Valid prompt and context-policy mutations.
  • Rejection of hidden-evaluator, permission, budget, and promotion-policy changes.
  • Composite artifact digest and provenance tests.
  • Fresh held-out evaluation and deterministic fixture tests.
  • Comparison against the unchanged baseline harness under equal budgets.
  • Resume and replay of a harness-evolution run.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: All mutation surfaces at once, unrestricted self-modification, automatic promotion to production, policy meta-evolution, and claims of general recursive self-improvement.

docs.title: Milestone 8.7: audited prior-candidate source inspection
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). Tracked by #150. This is an independent post-M8 follow-up, not an M8 closure gate, and it does not change M8.6 or M9.5.

The ordered program is M8.7.1 → M8.7.2 → M8.7.3 → M8.7.4 → M8.7.5:

  • [x] #155 — M8.7.1: proved the value of exact prior source using existing durable evidence in examples/agents/prior_source_inspection/.
  • [x] #158 — M8.7.2: shipped August 18, 2026. It locks the public, accounting, replay, and Git-neutral manifest contracts.
  • [x] #159 — M8.7.3: shipped August 18, 2026. It adds bounded audited source path listing and reads while source diff and history projection remain unavailable.
  • [x] #160 — M8.7.4: shipped August 18, 2026. It adds a canonical library-owned source diff.
  • [x] #161 — M8.7.5: shipped August 18, 2026. It projects authorized manifests into a disposable read-only Git history view.

Source access remains same-task, same-run, strictly prior, occurrence-based, bounded by the existing experience grant, and reconstructed from committed observations. Git is a presentation adapter, never durable identity or part of the candidate artifact. Cross-run libraries, semantic retrieval, whole-tree reads, and coordinator branches remain out of scope.

docs.title: M8.7.2 contract boundary
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). This stage published advanced durable vocabulary and protocol shape, not a callable source capability. M8.7.3 now implements listing and reading under that contract; M8.7.5 now completes the shipped program.

Historical annotation. M8.7.5 narrowly supersedes this stage's earlier “no new durable event” reservation: truthful replay of a pre-execution mount requires one SourceHistoryMounted fact. The locked reader APIs, accounting, identity and authority rules remain unchanged, including the no Git-mount usage category claim. This is a final-stage repair to M8.7's own locked projection contract, not general permission to reopen shipped milestones.

The scoped ExperienceReader declares these operations; listing and reading ship in M8.7.3 and canonical diffing ships in M8.7.4:

list_source_paths(artifact_ref, *, as_of=None, limit=None) -> SourcePathListing
read_source(artifact_ref, *, paths, as_of=None) -> SourceRead
diff_source(
    older_artifact_ref,
    newer_artifact_ref,
    *,
    paths=(),
    as_of=None,
) -> SourceDiff

Every target is an exact ExperienceRef(kind="artifact") occurrence. Shipped listing, reads, and diffs accept only SourceTree / utf8-tree-v1. ExperienceRequest admits the three operation names and an ordered paths tuple whose empty default is omitted canonically, preserving legacy schema-v3 bytes. Anything other than a tuple of strings is a Python shape error before auditing. Empty reads, duplicates, non-normalized paths, wrong reference kinds, invalid logical time, and inaccessible, missing, future, hidden, retracted, or cross-run content enter the normal audit lifecycle and produce the same opaque denial. One missing requested path atomically denies the complete read.

Authorization and artifact existence precede capacity resolution. Listing and reading reserve one result; diff reserves two. Missing complete result capacity uses the existing opaque exhaustion outcome. Record and character ceilings retain the largest deterministic prefix of complete paths, files, or diff entries—never partial source. Each retained entry charges one record and the character delta is exactly len(rendered). Listings render normalized lexicographic prefixes as compact JSON-string lines. Reads preserve requested order and render compact JSON Lines objects containing exactly path and source, with stable keys, Unicode preserved, and no trailing newline. Diff entries have added, deleted, or modified status and use meta-evolve-unified-diff/v1; M8.7.4 owns that shipped renderer.

SourcePathListing, SourceFile, SourceRead, SourceDiffEntry, and SourceDiff live only in meta_evolve.domain. Every result identifies its authorized occurrence and verified digest, retains complete entries, and carries canonical rendering, truncation state, and cumulative ExperienceUsage. The new standalone records use the current schema-v3 envelope; no migration or global schema bump occurs.

Existing PullAccess defaults remain unchanged. A source-sized profile is only an ordinary outer grant:

from meta_evolve.policies import PullAccess

SOURCE_ACCESS = PullAccess(
    max_operations=40,
    max_results=40,
    max_records=400,
    max_chars=256_000,
)

Human-facing accounting uses canonically ordered, non-zero ExperienceOperationUsage entries in this order: search, open, ancestors, siblings, compare, list_source_paths, read_source, then diff_source. Their dimension-wise sum equals RunExperienceUsage.pull. Manifest construction reuses audited operations, so there is no Git-mount category and no duplicate byte charge. M8.7.3 implements this derived view.

docs.title: M8.7.3 audited source listing and reads
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). AuditedExperienceReader now executes list_source_paths and read_source for exact, visible source-tree / utf8-tree-v1 artifact occurrences. At that stage diff_source remained fail-closed; M8.7.4 now ships it. Git projection, whole-tree reads, semantic retrieval, and cross-run access remain unshipped.

Resolution first proves the occurrence is visible in the same task and run at the effective strictly-prior boundary, then asks the artifact-store edge to revalidate its digest and decode its source tree. Missing, inaccessible, wrong-kind, and unsupported occurrences share one opaque denial. Durable corruption and infrastructure failures remain typed. Reads prove every path exists before reserving result capacity, so one missing path discloses and charges no source content.

One successful listing or read consumes one result. The largest prefix of complete entries fitting caller, record, and character bounds is retained; newlines between entries count, and no path or file is split. A zero-capacity prefix is a truncated success after its result charge. Operation- and result-ceiling exhaustion are durable, cumulative audit outcomes. Replay returns committed outcomes without live resolution, while durable loading independently reproduces every source result from its stored artifact.

Successful listing/read occurrences enter the existing observation ledger and may be cited in Proposal.derived_from; denied, exhausted, or missing-path attempts do not. RunExperienceUsage.by_operation exposes canonical non-zero application views whose dimension-wise sum equals RunExperienceUsage.pull.

Three Git-neutral durable values fix the future history presentation:

SourceHistoryBounds(max_ancestors, max_archive_members, max_chars)
SourceHistoryEntry(
    artifact_ref,
    digest,
    parent_refs,
    logical_step,
    proposal_ref,
    evaluation_ref,
    selection_rationale,
)
SourceHistoryManifest(format_version, head_ref, entries, bounds)

The format is source-history-manifest/v1; head_ref identifies the first entry. Artifact occurrence refs are unique even when their content digests match. All refs have declared kinds and one run, and parent refs remain inside the authorized manifest. Every entry retains the proposal, evaluation, logical step, digest, and rationale explaining its presence. Source bytes, Git IDs or refs, commit metadata, environment values, and repository layout are excluded.

M8.7.5 may present that same authorized history through this future adapter declaration:

meta.PatchProposer(
    edit,
    history=meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView(
        max_ancestors=...,
        max_archive_members=...,
        max_chars=...,
    ),
)

All history bounds are explicit. Experiment(experience=PullAccess(...)) remains the outer authority. At this stage the declaration added no implementation, root export, ninth Experiment field, run() overlay, artifact identity, Git authority, coordinator branch, or parallel proposer runtime.

docs.title: M8.7.4 canonical audited source diffs
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). AuditedExperienceReader.diff_source authorizes and verifies its older then newer exact occurrences through the M8.7.3 source edge before atomically reserving two results. Both operands must be visible, same-task/run, strictly prior source-tree / utf8-tree-v1 occurrences. Successful diffs retain both occurrence refs and verified digests; the observation ledger admits those refs in operand order.

The pure meta-evolve-unified-diff/v1 renderer compares the sorted changed-path union, with an optional filter that cannot alter output order. It normalizes CRLF and CR to LF while retaining final-terminator state, uses a deterministic Myers line diff with deletion-before-insertion ties, emits three context lines, and merges changes separated by at most six unchanged lines. JSON-encoded file operands, uniform hunk ranges, missing-final-newline markers, complete per-path headers and hunks, and no trailing newline make rendering independent of Git, subprocesses, and platforms.

Record and character ceilings retain the largest ordered prefix of complete entries after the two-result reservation; a first oversized entry is a successful truncated zero-record result, while an empty canonical diff is not truncated. Replay returns committed outcomes without resolving artifacts. Folding validates operand visibility, result shape, canonical ordering, rendering, and exact usage; durable loading independently resolves both stored artifacts and reconstructs the complete expected result. Schema version 3, root exports, Experiment, coordinator dispatch, and proposer constructors are unchanged. At this stage Git history projection remained reserved for M8.7.5.

docs.title: M8.7.5 authorized read-only Git history
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView adds an optional PatchProposer(history=...) capability with required ancestor, archive-member, and character bounds. It uses the declared pull grant to audit a complete selected-parent listing, canonical metadata search, ancestor traversal, and complete additional-tree reads. Selection is parent first, then breadth-first causal ancestors, then archive order; duplicate occurrences are removed by first occurrence while equal digests remain distinct.

The resulting source-history-manifest/v1 is committed once as SourceHistoryMounted before callback execution. The fact has no usage delta, operation category, or derivation authority. Replay drives the identical audited prefix from committed outcomes, and durable loading revalidates both the source observations and the reconstructed manifest without retaining Git objects.

Git objects, refs, configuration, index, attributes, hooks, and home live in a disposable external sidecar. The callback receives a meta_evolve.ports.WorkspaceSession with the materialized root, a complete controlled subprocess environment, and the committed manifest. HEAD is the selected parent, causal parents are ordinary commits, and retained archive members have deterministic ephemeral refs. The frozen sidecar is disposed before capture; any direct callback mutation of the source workspace is a PolicyViolation.

GitHistoryView is adapter-only, and changing its version or bounds changes the configured proposer identity. There is no root export, run() overlay, Experiment field, coordinator branch, whole-tree reader operation, cross-run access, semantic retrieval, persistent Git identity, or independent agent runtime.

docs.title: Milestone 9: policy artifacts and meta-evolution
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 6, 2026). The canonical deterministic example is examples/research/policy_evolution/. M9 depends on the contracts shipped in M8.1–M8.5; it does not depend on #124 or the M8.6 live proof.

docs.title: Executable subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] M9.0: lock dependency, authority, reuse, aggregation, and namespace decisions before implementation.
  • [x] M9.1: ship search-policy / policy-manifest-v1, two fixed mutation surfaces, neutral mutation contracts, and four-surface conformance.
  • [x] M9.2: register trusted candidate-policy@1, publish SearchProgramTests, and verify durable reconstruction.
  • [x] M9.3: ship portable policy episodes, explicit splits, captured inner run references, exact reuse/resume boundaries, and nested usage separation.
  • [x] M9.4: aggregate all outcomes and strictly compare separate seed-only held-out outer runs without granting promotion authority.
  • [x] M9.5: run the deterministic durable flagship with development quality 6.0 → 7.0 → 8.0 and held-out aggregate 13.5 → 15.5.

docs.title: M9.0 executable contract
docs.text:
• meta_evolve.policy owns artifact-domain values; meta_evolve.policies continues to own executable presets.
  • Only generic MutationApplication[SurfaceT] and MutationSurface[MutationT, SurfaceT] move to meta_evolve.mutation; harness-specific mutations and parameters stay namespaced under harness.
  • Policy episodes and comparisons remain domain-specific peers of harness equivalents. No generic episode/comparison framework exists without a third domain demonstrating it.
  • An episode's existing content-addressed RunId is its sole cache identity. Aggregates are recomputed; evaluator identity covers the exact suite, split, scoring, aggregation, budgets, and environment.
  • Fresh development forbids non-identical reuse, while an exact completed run may reopen. Held-out execution always uses a new empty namespace and bypasses reuse.
  • Any failed, incomplete, or missing episode makes the aggregate non-rankable while retaining partial results and typed failures.
  • Inner trials and evaluations remain inner usage. Only tokens, monetary spend, and elapsed time roll into the enclosing evaluation's Usage.
  • Candidates cannot control tasks, seeds, proposers, evaluators, environments, budgets, split membership, caching, aggregation, promotion, or executable policy source.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Evaluate search or update policies as artifacts by measuring the improvement episodes they produce on held-out task distributions.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Two versioned PolicyArtifacts each control fresh inner-loop optimization episodes across training and held-out tasks. An outer policy compares their quality, cost, robustness, and failure rates under equal nested budgets.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Serializable PolicyArtifact with declared interfaces and mutation boundaries.
  • Nested run/episode relationships and separate inner/outer budgets.
  • Task-distribution artifacts and held-out evaluation splits.
  • Existing RunId cache identity and explicit leakage boundaries.
  • Aggregation of quality, cost, uncertainty, and failure metrics across episodes.
  • External promotion decision for policy candidates.
  • examples/research/policy_evolution/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• A policy candidate cannot inspect held-out results before its evaluation episode permits them.
  • Inner-loop events retain their own lineage while linking to the outer policy evaluation.
  • Cache hits are valid only when task, artifact, policy, evaluator, environment, seed, and relevant budget semantics match.
  • Promotion uses fresh evidence across multiple tasks or seeds rather than a policy's self-report.
  • Budget exhaustion in an inner episode does not consume undeclared outer authority.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Compare two deterministic policy artifacts across several task fixtures.
  • Nested budget accounting and exhaustion.
  • Held-out leakage rejection.
  • Cache-key correctness and invalidation.
  • Episode aggregation with failed and incomplete runs.
  • Replay from an outer decision to every supporting inner evaluation.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Learned schedulers, model-weight training inside the kernel, autonomous authority changes, production deployment, and claims that improvement generalizes beyond measured tasks.

docs.title: Milestone 9.5: advanced search
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 17, 2026; #144, #148). M9.5 adds a bounded advanced-search slice after shipped M9, now that the M8 closure gate has passed. Its M9.5.1 archive-compatibility prerequisite, M9.5.2 specialist-retention slice, M9.5.3 tree-search slice, and M9.5.4 unified comparison are all complete. The local-author M10 does not depend on it; trusted distribution and federation move to M11 and M12. Tracked by #144. This interstitial milestone is distinct from M9's historical M9.5 executable substep, which assembled the already-shipped policy-evolution flagship.

docs.title: Ordered subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] #146 — M9.5.1: lock primary-objective defaults, frontier metric coverage, multi-member archive transitions, deterministic ties, named randomness, and history-derived policy statistics.
  • [x] #147 — M9.5.2: ship replayable per-key frontier evolution with deterministic winners, ownership-weighted parent selection, durable reconstruction, and focused equal-budget evidence.
  • [x] #145 — M9.5.3: ship replayable value-directed tree search with fixed progressive widening, best-descendant backup, durable reconstruction, and focused equal-budget evidence.
  • [x] #148 — M9.5.4: publish the deterministic equal-budget five-policy comparison after both concrete policies landed.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Demonstrate genuine multi-generation evolution through two concrete, replayable search policies: GEPA-style per-key frontier evolution and UCT-style tree allocation with best-descendant backup. Both must pass the existing search-program conformance suite and outperform the appropriate baseline on deterministic, equal-budget fixtures.

Specialists and TreeSearch are the shipped canonical names for per-metric specialist retention and value-directed tree allocation. Both use the policy namespace rather than adding a root export:

from meta_evolve.policies import Specialists, TreeSearch

Specialists(
    metrics=("case:0", "case:1", "case:2"),
    max_trials=20,
)

TreeSearch(
    max_trials=100,
    exploration=2**0.5,
)

BestOfN remains the one-generation equal-budget sampling control. M9.5 does not reopen the closed novelty, surrogate, or plateau-escalation proposals in #16, #17, or #18.

docs.title: Contract boundary
docs.text:
• Shipped default ranking, stopping, and incumbent selection use Task.objectives[0]; successful evaluations may retain additional metrics.
  • Specialists binds a fixed ordered metric-key tuple. Every successful candidate must contain each configured key; extra metrics are ignored and a missing key is invalid search history.
  • Archive membership remains authoritative. Existing records keep replaying; membership deltas may remove several members without a new schema version or removed_member_ids field. evicted_artifact_id is None for zero or multiple removals and identifies the member for exactly one removal.
  • Per-key winners, ownership weights, tree visits, subtree values, and normalization inputs reconstruct from durable history. M9.5 deliberately accepts derived-state recomputation cost instead of adding hidden caches.
  • Stable tie rules and named decision randomness make replay and cross-process reconstruction deterministic.
  • Failed evaluations remain typed outcomes: they never become frontier members or synthetic low tree rewards, though failed tree attempts still count as visits.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text:
M9.5.2 adds a focused deterministic scenario beside the existing scalar comparison: BestOfN, Population, and Specialists share the same task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and trial limit. Population evaluates then evicts an aggregate-weak per-case specialist; Specialists retains and expands it into the aggregate winner. The report pins score, lineage, parent sequence, evaluation and failure counts, and exact usage.

M9.5.3 adds a separate deterministic delayed-reward scenario: Greedy and TreeSearch share the same task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and explicit trial limit. Greedy's incumbent selection follows the immediately attractive branch to a plateau; TreeSearch's fixed widening also materializes the weaker delayed branch, and deterministic UCT descent revisits and expands it into the winner. The report pins score, lineage, parent sequence, evaluation and failure counts, and exact usage.

M9.5.4 adds one credential-free command, examples/learn/policy_comparison/advanced_search.py, that runs BestOfN, Greedy, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch on both fixtures above under the same task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and explicit trial allowance, with equality verified pairwise through the existing Run.compare() gate. On the specialist fixture, capacity-matched Population evicts the aggregate-weak specialist that Specialists retains and expands into the aggregate winner 10, which equal-budget BestOfN never reaches. On the delayed-reward fixture, Greedy plateaus at the immediately attractive score 5 while TreeSearch revisits the weaker delayed branch and reaches its descendant 10. Every result's report pins primary score, lineage shape and depth, every selected parent, evaluation and failure counts, archive behavior, and exact resource usage; the other policy results stay visible without broadening either pair-specific claim.

Replay equivalence is a conformance invariant. The milestone's behavioral evidence is improvement on these controlled equal-budget fixtures.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Existing archive records replay, valid multi-removal transitions validate, and malformed membership deltas fail deterministically.
  • Frontier specialists remain selectable, one candidate may displace several obsolete members, missing dimensions fail, and extra dimensions are valid.
  • Frontier replay, resume, and cross-process reconstruction select identical parents.
  • Tree tests pin node selection, visit accounting, progressive widening, deterministic normalization, direction handling, and Q-value backup.
  • Failure-heavy tree branches remain representable without fabricated scores.
  • Both presets pass conformance, replay, and resume suites.
  • Both deterministic fixtures demonstrate the intended later-generation or delayed-reward advantage under equal budgets.
  • The unified five-policy comparison holds every external control equal within each fixture and reports complete structured evidence for every policy.
  • Examples, API references, guides, architecture, programming model, and implementation plan agreed before the status changed to Shipped.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Pareto archives, novelty search, islands, learned allocation, live-provider evidence, and extracting ParentSelector, Archive, BackupRule, or similar protocols. Revisit a shared protocol only after both concrete policies expose a repeated independently testable seam.

docs.title: Milestone 10: local author API and inspection experience
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 14, 2026; #149). This milestone does not depend on M8.6 or M9.5.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make local experiments easier to declare and pace, search algorithms easier to author, failures easier to diagnose, and artifact evolution easier to inspect. The public narrative is: proposers create candidates, evaluators judge them, search decides what to try next, and Meta-Evolve records the entire process. The subordinate M10.0 design record owns the six journey definitions, vocabulary decisions, and measured scorecard. The core remains dependency-free. An optional browser remains read-only and loopback-only, with no execution, resume, cancellation, promotion, deletion, remote collaboration, or distributed-operations authority.

docs.title: Ordered subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] #151 — M10.0: lock the local-author journeys, vocabulary, friction budget, compatibility promises, and bounded exception to the historical dashboard warning.
  • [x] #152 — M10.1: Shipped. An immutable typed Experiment declaration preserves the existing keyword-based run call and dictionary CLI compatibility through 1.x with a DeprecationWarning.
  • [x] #165 — M10.2: Shipped. The minimal improve() callable path lowers exactly through Task, Experiment, bounded Greedy, and local run().
  • [x] #164 — M10.3: Shipped. Functional incumbent refinement is available through a curated @meta.search façade over the full SearchProgram.next() protocol, with immutable identity-visible configuration and shared Greedy lowering.
  • [x] #153 — M10.4: Shipped. One immutable aggregate Run.inspect() read model covers complete, incomplete, rankable, and unrankable histories through exactly one authoritative validated replay.
  • [x] #154 — M10.5: Shipped. Genuinely read-only durable storage supports immutable inspection and exact per-run committed stream versions while observing live WAL commits.
  • [x] #166 — M10.6: Shipped. Paced and resumable Session execution is the sole synchronous dispatcher; run() and resume() exhaust it without changing durable history.
  • [x] #156 — M10.7: Shipped. An optional server-rendered local run browser uses only public inspection, comparison, read-only storage, and version APIs. One dedicated thread owns storage access; exact-version bounded caches avoid unnecessary replay; loopback-only routes expose no execution or mutation authority.
  • [x] #157 — M10.8: Shipped. Frozen-payload presentation, bounded direct-parent diffs, exact canonical attachments, occurrence-aware browser pages, optional custom-codec reconstruction, and the accessible visual system complete the read-only artifact history. Notebook HTML and screenshot automation belong to the explicit post-M10 presentation follow-up below.

The dependency order is:

M10.0 ─┬→ M10.1 → M10.2
       ├→ M10.3
       ├→ M10.4 ─┬→ M10.6 ← M10.1
       │          └→ M10.7 → M10.8
       └→ M10.5 ──────┘

Each child shipped through one focused PR.

docs.title: Acceptance gate
docs.text:
• M10.0 publishes the six measured journeys and decisions in the design record, meets both functional-search reduction thresholds, adds no proposed API, and preserves the uncreated examples/research/trusted_workers/ reservation.
  • Dictionary CLI factories remain supported through 1.x; M10.1 owns introducing the typed alternative and its DeprecationWarning.
  • Equivalent beginner, typed, keyword, and functional-search declarations retain the required honest identities and identical durable facts, decisions, stop reasons, and effective budgets where equivalence is claimed.
  • Functional search exposes only opaque seed/incumbent handles, immutable declared configuration, expand(), and stop(); captured configuration may not remain invisible to identity. Decision narration follows the #164 child contract.
  • One stable inspection view handles successful, failed, incomplete, and unrankable runs without winner-only assumptions. It exposes resolved defaults and immutable decision views reusable by paced execution.
  • Read-only storage performs no migration or filesystem mutation and exposes the maximum committed event sequence when supported.
  • Session fixes authority and budgets at start, commits and completes one decision per step, returns the committed terminal decision idempotently, and preserves byte-identical history across uninterrupted and resumed execution.
  • The optional browser imports only public inspection and storage APIs, polls versions before replay, binds only to loopback, and exposes no mutable or operational controls or imports of execution surfaces.
  • Occurrence identity remains distinct from content digest; artifact views and diffs never execute stored active content. Notebook HTML representations and screenshot automation belong to the post-M10 presentation follow-up.
  • Examples, public exports, tests, and canonical documentation match each surface before its status changes to Shipped.
  • The documentation entrance labels the scorecard as an authoring-friction measurement of proposed syntax, never optimization or runtime evidence.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Provider transcripts that were not durably recorded; remote or distributed dashboards; execution or governance controls; authentication claims; and frontier or tree presentation before M9.5 policies ship. Outer/inner loops, generations, and episodes remain relative explanatory terms rather than new core types. Deferred and rejected author surfaces are recorded once in the M10.0 design record.

docs.title: Post-M10 presentation follow-up
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This follow-up owns notebook HTML representations built on the shipped inert presentation contract, plus browser screenshot automation or visual-regression evidence. It depends on the safe presentation boundary shipped in M10.8, is not part of the M10 closure gate, and adds no current notebook-rendering claim. Implementation requires its own future acceptance gate before either capability may be described as shipped.

docs.title: Issue #143 P1: monetary cost as a first-class resource
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Tracked by #143. First-class monetary usage: spend_micros in Usage/Budget and post-hoc enforcement. The field is absent at its default, so spend-free streams keep their existing bytes and the durable schema stays at v3 — a bump would have invalidated every stored pull-experience run, whose rendered text is byte-compared on replay. Issue #143 owns the requirements, and every acceptance criterion is recorded against the evidence that settles it. This work is independent of M11; M11's reservation and settlement deliverable is this work's P2, which adds the reservation-based hard cap that P1 deliberately omits.

docs.title: Milestone 11: trusted concurrency and distribution
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #10.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Execute work concurrently on trusted workers without corrupting history, budgets, population state, or promotion decisions.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Several worker processes claim bounded work through leases. Workers finish out of wall-clock order, one lease expires, and one result is submitted twice. The reconstructed logical run preserves one trial across delivery retries, contains one accepted outcome, and has correct budget accounting.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Durable work states and atomic lease acquisition, renewal, expiration, cancellation, and completion.
  • WorkAttempt identities that remain distinct from their logical Trial and WorkItem.
  • Worker capability and resource declarations.
  • Idempotent result submission and retry policy.
  • Atomic budget reservation and settlement.
  • Scheduler matching work requirements to trusted workers.
  • Explicit consistency rules for durable facts, leases, heuristic frontier statistics, and promotion.
  • Multi-process load and fault-injection test harness.
  • examples/research/trusted_workers/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• At most one completion has logical effect for an idempotency key.
  • Expired workers cannot overwrite an accepted result.
  • Out-of-order completion does not create future-information leakage.
  • Durable events and evaluations are strongly inserted; heuristic statistics may tolerate documented staleness.
  • Promotion and budget accounting use authoritative state.
  • Local and distributed runs preserve the same task, artifact, trial, work, evaluation, and event semantics.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Competing lease claims.
  • Lease renewal and expiration races.
  • Duplicate and late result submission.
  • Worker termination during execution and evaluation.
  • Atomic budget reservation under concurrency.
  • Projection rebuild after out-of-order events.
  • Load test with simulated trusted workers before paid agent fleets.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Arbitrary untrusted community code, Byzantine workers, public federation, reputation economies, and universal strong consistency.

docs.title: Milestone 12: contributed and federated network
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #11 and dependent on M11's trusted-worker boundary.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Allow independent installations to contribute and exchange authorized agents, evaluators, artifacts, evidence, and experience subgraphs with verifiable provenance.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Two Meta-Evolve installations exchange a signed, policy-filtered experience bundle. The receiving installation verifies identity and content, imports only authorized records, preserves source provenance and restrictions, independently evaluates a promoted candidate, and processes a later retraction.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Signed manifests for contributors, agents, evaluators, tasks, environments, and artifact schemas.
  • Scoped identities and task-specific trust policies.
  • Canonical export/import format for policy-filtered experience subgraphs.
  • Verification of signatures, content digests, schema compatibility, causal closure, and access labels.
  • Provenance, licensing, embargo, attribution, and retraction propagation through derivation edges.
  • Independent or redundant evaluation for promotion-sensitive results.
  • Minimal dispute and reputation projections based on recorded evidence.
  • examples/research/federated_exchange/ using two local installations.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• Import never grants broader access than the source export policy and receiving trust policy allow.
  • Missing private ancestors can be represented by verifiable redacted references without fabricating lineage.
  • Invalid signatures, digests, schemas, or causal references are rejected.
  • Imported evaluations are evidence, not automatic local promotion.
  • Retractions and permission changes identify dependent artifacts, datasets, skills, and checkpoints.
  • Operators may keep private events while publishing permitted claims and artifacts.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Successful signed export/import between two installations.
  • Tampered payload, signature, digest, and causal-edge rejection.
  • Private, embargoed, and redacted source handling.
  • Conflicting evaluator results and independent verification.
  • Retraction propagation through derived records.
  • Duplicate import idempotency and schema-version negotiation.
  • Threat-model review covering code execution, evaluator collusion, poisoning, sybil behavior, reward hacking, and correlated replication.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Token economies, unrestricted peer-to-peer execution, global consensus, claims that containers alone secure untrusted code, and scientific validity without domain-governed evidence and replication.

docs.title: Architecture gate across all milestones
docs.text:
The following test should remain true throughout development:

new use case
  = artifact codec and schema
  + task and evaluator
  + agent or mutator
  + search/context configuration
  + optional infrastructure adapters

new use case
  ≠ coordinator branch
  ≠ new durable semantics
  ≠ bypassed authority boundary

When a new domain does not fit, first determine whether it needs a general protocol capability or whether it lies outside evaluated artifact-improvement loops. The kernel should grow only for the former.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
This is the canonical contract for the shipped public API available from the current package. The generated API reference owns signatures and parameter details; the guides below own task-oriented usage. Milestone 9 is shipped. The deterministic M8.1–M8.5 implementation is in the package. M8.6 is closed: the first authorized official-SDK capture failed schema validation before returning a native mutation, and a later authorized run through a second provider boundary returned complete manifests that reached native mutation decoding and the trusted successor boundary. Both captures are retained unimproved. That closes the gate's named blocker and claims nothing about statistical generalization.

M10.1's immutable Experiment declaration and M10.2's minimal improve() callable are Shipped. M10.3's bounded @search author façade, M10.4's winner-independent Run.inspect() aggregate, M10.5's read-only durable storage, M10.6's paced and resumable Session, M10.7's optional browser, and M10.8's artifact presentation are also Shipped. The parent M10 milestone is complete as of August 14, 2026.

Milestone 5 is complete: immutable source trees, exact patches, bounded processes, and independent command evaluation compose through the same callable path. Milestone 7 completes the cross-domain extension boundary. User-owned SDK wrappers use that path; no first-party provider adapter is shipped.

docs.title: The smallest useful mental model
docs.text:
Start with an artifact to change, a function that proposes revisions, and an independent function that measures them. Search chooses which parent to expand; authorized feedback supplies recorded observations. Limits remain external to the candidate. The complete parser lesson includes installation, source, execution, and saved results on one page.

This excerpt is the canonical parser declaration. SEED is Python source, evaluate grades development cases, and lesson_identity records the code fingerprint. client is the example's user-owned SDK wrapper:

Parser experiment · extracted from the canonical script
def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )
Role Declaration Artifact / seed seed supplies the starting source Proposer proposer suggests the next version Task / evaluator and objectives Task owns grading and the satisfaction threshold Search Greedy allows at most three revisions Feedback / experience AncestorsOnly explicitly authorizes recorded development evidence External limits Model request settings, grader execution limits, fixed cases, and storage

The routing lesson changes the source artifact to a prompt and uses a response model inside evaluation. Python still grades against independent answers. The same loop records versions, results, usage, and decisions.

For a minimal run, improve() accepts seed, proposer, evaluator, and trials. It lowers to Task, Experiment, and bounded Greedy search. Use the explicit declaration above when adding objectives, feedback, context, or other experiment settings; improve() does not automatically send feedback. The source-compatible declaration-keyword form of run() remains available for 1.x compatibility; new examples use the typed declaration.

For an existing caller using declaration keywords, the equivalent spelling is:

1.x compatibility · with the same declared experiment
declared = experiment(client)
result = meta.run(
    task=declared.task,
    seed=declared.seed,
    proposer=declared.proposer,
    search=declared.search,
    context=declared.context,
)

Experiment owns the eight declaration fields and defaults. Storage, mode, and a narrowing call-level budget are execution overlays on run(), never experiment fields.

The returned Run is both the result and the query surface for aggregate inspection, trials, lineage, evidence, usage, failures, summaries, and comparisons. Usage.spend_micros accepts an integer billed amount or None for unknown; its default 0 describes known free work. Unknown totals remain unknown, and monetary ceilings stop further work when spend cannot be verified. Estimates remain evidence. See evaluation and budgets. Safe frozen-payload presentation, direct-parent diff rules, and exact current canonical-payload-v1 bytes are specified by the browser guide.

run() exhausts the same synchronous Session available for paced execution. Session fixes the experiment, effective budget, components, and authority at start. Each step() commits one decision or completes one owed by recovery, then returns its immutable DecisionView; it accepts no injected decision. Bootstrap is complete before Session.start() returns and is not a policy step.

Durable storage has two independent axes: is_durable means committed facts live on durable media, while is_read_only means this handle has no commit or execution authority. Storage.durable(path) is durable and writable; Storage.read_only(path) is durable and read-only. Storage.run_version(id) returns the maximum committed event sequence, or 0 when that well-formed id has no events. The latter is a polling result, not authoritative run loading: opening a required missing run still raises RunNotFound.

docs.title: Canonical public surface
docs.text:
The curated reference partitions shipped root exports into four tiers. Root imports are public; kernel records remain internal unless a guide explicitly describes an extension protocol.

The constructible harness family stays under meta_evolve.harness: HarnessArtifact, HarnessMutation, MutationSurface, TextParam, PolicyParam, MutationApplication, portable repository episodes, comparison views, and export views. Only compare_harnesses, export_harness, and load_harness are root conveniences.

The neutral MutationApplication and MutationSurface contracts live under meta_evolve.mutation; harness keeps compatibility re-exports. The data-only M9 family lives under meta_evolve.policy: PolicyArtifact, its two fixed surfaces and mutation, CandidatePolicy, portable episodes/suites, captured outcomes/evaluations, and comparison views. compare_policies is the single root convenience.

docs.title: Shipped guides
docs.text:
• Runs and results — the callable story and query views.
  • Evaluation and budgets — objectives, evidence, usage, and typed failures.
  • Learning from experience — no memory, pushed context, audited pull, and derivation.
  • Durability — storage, reopen, recovery, and resume.
  • SDK integration — user-owned callable wrappers and audited tools.
  • Command line — run, list, inspect, resume, compare, and browse.
  • Local run browser — optional server-rendered read-only inspection.
  • Extensions — codecs, registries, component identity, and conformance.
  • Policy evolution — trusted policy artifacts, nested capture, and held-out comparison.

docs.title: Execution profiles
docs.text: local accepts live Python components and defaults to isolated in-memory storage. durable-local requires durable storage plus registered, reconstructible components and records enough identity to resume honestly through either Session.resume() or resume(). The proposed distributed profile is design material, not a shipped execution mode.

docs.title: Authority and failure boundary
docs.text:
Candidates may propose artifact content. They cannot change the evaluator, effective budget, permissions, hidden data, audit history, or promotion rule. Invalid output, proposer/evaluator failure, timeout, exhaustion, policy violation, and infrastructure failure remain typed, inspectable outcomes. A failure with no valid measurement is never ranked as a low score.

Harness candidates receive a second, trusted check after codec encoding and before artifact creation. The built-in harness codec compares the encoded successor with its one parent and rejects changed component references, interfaces, parameter names or types as PolicyViolation; malformed and no-op transitions are InvalidOutput. Wrapper-side mutation helpers are convenience, not authority.

M8.7.3 ships bounded list_source_paths and read_source; M8.7.4 ships canonical diff_source over exact, prior same-task/run occurrences. Successful observations may be cited in proposal derivation. M8.7.5 lets PatchProposer project a bounded committed manifest through adapter-only GitHistoryView; its callback receives meta_evolve.ports.WorkspaceSession. Experiment, root exports, run() overlays, authority, artifact identities, and the coordinator remain unchanged. This page owns the public surface; the M8.7 contract records limits and acceptance history.

The shipped declaration is:

meta.PatchProposer(
    edit,
    history=meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView(
        max_ancestors=4,
        max_archive_members=2,
        max_chars=128_000,
    ),
)

All bounds are required non-negative keywords. history=None preserves prior identity and behavior. In a history-enabled callback, defaulted ProposerContext.workspace contains root, the complete controlled subprocess environment, and the committed history manifest.

docs.title: TreeSearch and value-directed tree allocation
docs.text: TreeSearch (meta_evolve.policies.TreeSearch, not a root export) reconstructs one node per materialized artifact occurrence from durable history. It widens a node with a new child while child_count < ceil(sqrt(node_visits)) and otherwise descends by normalized best-descendant UCT, breaking exact ties by ascending artifact occurrence ID. docs.title: The common experimental substrate
docs.text: All labs consume a structural SessionRunner. The repository supplies orchestration and deterministic injected-runner tests; users supply any live SDK wrapper. The wrapper owns authentication, structured decoding, tools, permissions, model configuration, and provider telemetry.

docs.title: What is frozen and what may change
docs.text: The fixture questions, documents, evaluator-only answers, schemas, and session arithmetic are frozen. Candidate prompts and recipes may change. The wrapper declaration and all behavior-affecting configuration must be recorded before a live run.

docs.title: Leakage boundary
docs.text: Solver views contain only public document ids, titles, dates, and text. Gold answers, source URLs, split roles, evaluation rules, permissions, budgets, and promotion decisions remain outside candidate authority.

docs.title: Failure and scoring semantics
docs.text: Malformed structured output, missing candidates, timeout, exhaustion, SDK or infrastructure failure, and protected-control edits are typed and unrankable. They are never converted into a low score. Deterministic graders alone produce rankable measurements.

docs.title: Evidence, lineage, and identity
docs.text: Each session retains its label, decoded value or typed failure, wrapper evidence, token and elapsed usage, and experience counters. Derived artifacts name their source evidence. A wrapper configuration change changes declared identity and prevents uncontrolled comparison.

docs.title: How the shared components actually work
docs.text: UserSdkSessionRunner invokes a user-provided proposer inside an ordinary one-trial meta.run(). A successful wrapper returns ProposalResult, puts the schema-decoded value in sdk.structured-output evidence, and reports only shared token and elapsed usage. The lab validates that value again before using it.

docs.title: How to run the curriculum
docs.text:
Create an opt-in driver outside the shipped examples. Implement build_agent(request), identify its declaration, and pass it to UserSdkSessionRunner; then call run_selected. Review the maximum call count, SDK permissions, and spending limits before setting META_EVOLVE_LIVE_SDK=1.

No official provider capture is pending. Users may perform one authorized run with their own wrapper. Any published capture must identify the wrapper declaration and preserve ties, failures, null results, and regressions honestly. The notebooks contain illustrative code and no fabricated live output.

docs.title: Start here: improve a duration parser
docs.text:
Meta-Evolve is a declarative Python library for evaluated evolution and meta-evolution over versioned artifacts. You define what can change and how to measure it; Meta-Evolve runs the search and records its history. Start with code, then apply the same loop to a routing prompt.

Use the same pattern for prompts, code, skills, harnesses, and search procedures. The applications overview explains the broader uses.

Status: Experimental/live-only. Offline checks cover the seed, SDK boundary, and saved runs. Live execution requires your OpenAI SDK and API key; no model result has been captured yet.

Suppose a time-tracking tool accepts "90s", but users also enter "1h30m" or "2 minutes". You want to improve the parser while keeping its behavior testable. The candidate is Python source text. A model proposes a replacement; Python checks the replacement against answers that the experiment owns.

Download the three-file parser bundle. All three complete files are also expandable below; no repository checkout or hidden helpers are needed:

File Responsibility parser.py Starting source, subprocess grader, experiment, and saved results parser_cases.py Contract, 40 development checks, and 12 separate final checks openai_client.py OpenAI request settings, output validation, and accounting

docs.title: Define what correct means
docs.text:
The contract supplied to the proposer
CONTRACT = """Implement parse_seconds(text: str) -> int.
1. Accept only nonnegative ASCII integer quantities (0-9).
2. Units: s/sec/secs/second/seconds, m/min/mins/minute/minutes,
   h/hr/hrs/hour/hours; return the total in seconds.
3. Accept one or more quantity-unit pairs, case-insensitive, with optional
   whitespace before, between, or after tokens; repeated units add together.
4. Raise ValueError for everything else: empty input, decimals, signs,
   colon notation, unsupported units, missing quantities/units, or junk.
"""

Units can repeat in any order: "1m2m" means 180 seconds. "01s" means 1 second. Whitespace may separate pairs or quantities and units; it cannot split a number ("1 2s"). Plural spelling does not depend on the quantity. Consume every input completely, including rejecting junk after an otherwise valid pair.

Input Required result Why it matters "1s" 1 Basic seconds "2min" 120 Conversion and abbreviations "1h30m" 5400 Compound duration without spaces " 2 H " 7200 Whitespace and case "0h0m0s" 0 Zero is valid "1.5h" Raise ValueError Decimal quantities are outside the contract "1h junk" Raise ValueError Reject partially valid input

These hand-curated checks cover spellings, compounds, whitespace, case, zero, and malformed inputs. The 12 distinct final inputs are withheld from search and feedback. They remain visible in source for review; separation is experimental discipline, not secrecy from a repository reader.

docs.title: Run the seed check
docs.text:
Already using a repository checkout? From its root, uv sync --locked followed by uv run python examples/learn/llm/parser.py --dry-run runs the same seed check shown below. The standalone installation path follows.

Use Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Save parser.zip in a new working folder together with the matching source package, open a terminal there, and run:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip
python -m zipfile -e parser.zip .

The source package is generated with this documentation build. Keep the three extracted files together. The SDK is needed only for the live run below.

The seed supports just s and m, without spaces. It is a plausible incomplete implementation, rather than an intentionally broken program:

Starting artifact · parser.py
SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    """Parse a whole number of seconds or minutes."""
    import re
    match = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+)(s|m)", text)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("expected seconds or minutes")
    quantity, unit = match.groups()
    return int(quantity) * (60 if unit == "m" else 1)
'''

Run the real grader with no model requests, SDK installation, or credentials:

python parser.py --dry-run
# Output:
# Dry run: no SDK requests; only the seed is evaluated.
# Seed: 17/40 development cases
# '1s': {'value': 1}; expected 1
# '2sec': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 2
# '3secs': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 3
# '4second': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 4
# '5seconds': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 5
# '1m': {'value': 60}; expected 60

The tested output measures this seed: 17 passing checks give a score of 0.425. Correctly rejecting invalid input counts as a pass. The command prints six observations; the evaluator produces one for each of the 40 checks.

docs.title: Assemble the improvement loop
docs.text:
The proposer asks for a revision. The evaluator measures that revision against independent answers. Search chooses the parent and when to stop; feedback supplies the selected parent's already recorded development checks. The starting source is the seed. These roles become the following declaration.

This extracted function comes from parser.py. CONTRACT is shown above; evaluate grades the source, and lesson_identity records the implementation fingerprint. Their complete definitions are expandable on this page.

Experiment and explicit development feedback · parser.py
def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )
Role This experiment Artifact / seed The source string in SEED; each replacement is a new version Proposer propose sends the current source, full contract, and authorized observations to client.generate Task / evaluator and objectives evaluate runs development inputs and returns their passing fraction; Maximize requests a score of 1.0 Search Greedy expands the best measured candidate, with at most three revisions Feedback / experience AncestorsOnly supplies committed ancestor records; the proposer extracts only the selected parent's case observations External limits Fixed cases, independent answers, child limits, model settings, attempt limit, and storage location

For one revision, Meta-Evolve selects the parent and supplies its recorded observations. Your proposer asks for new source. Your evaluator executes that source in a fresh child process and grades it in the parent process. Meta-Evolve records the artifact and results, then decides whether to expand it next.

The model cannot change the experiment's answers, search limit, or satisfaction threshold. Evaluator feedback reaches the proposer through committed history.

docs.title: Improvement, ties, and regressions
docs.text:
The seed is evaluated before any revision. A perfect seed stops immediately; a revision that passes all 40 development checks also stops the search. Otherwise the loop can try up to three revisions, for at most four development evaluations and three model requests. The 12 final checks use Python only.

A tie keeps the earlier best occurrence. A worse revision remains in history but does not replace the parent used for the next proposal. best().value can therefore return an earlier revision or the seed. A final-check failure never triggers another revision. No live score, improvement, or generalization is promised by these rules.

docs.title: Inspect the grader
docs.text:
This excerpt turns the child's returned values into independent measurements. cases contains the evaluator's expected answers; rows contains the child's observed answers. None in an expected case means it must raise ValueError.

Case grading · excerpt from evaluate in parser.py
    checks = tuple(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="duration-case", data={
        "input": text, "expected": expected, "actual": row,
        "passed": row == ({"error": "ValueError"} if expected is None else {"value": expected}),
    }) for (text, expected), row in zip(cases, rows))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(checks)},
        evidence=checks, usage=usage,
    )

The parent compares actual values with expected answers and sends only inputs to the child. Wrong answers lower the passing fraction; execution faults stay typed:

What happened Recorded result Wrong integer, return type, or exception for an input An observed failed case; the evaluation remains rankable Source cannot be parsed, required callable is absent, or output protocol is malformed InvalidOutput, with no score Source fails during module initialization EvaluatorFailure, with no score Execution exceeds its wall or CPU limit TimeoutFailure, with no score Child output exceeds its limit ResourceExhausted, with no score The evaluator cannot create a workspace or start Python InfrastructureFailure, with no score

Each evaluation uses a new temporary directory and isolated Python invocation. The child gets a minimal environment without OPENAI_API_KEY, a three-second wall limit, a two-second CPU limit, and at most 65,536 bytes of combined output. The parent reads at most that much output and cleans up the process group. Successful evaluations retain case observations; failed executions retain bounded process output when available. Proposal usage survives a later grading failure.

This is trusted development execution. The child can still access the host filesystem and network; a fresh directory and stripped environment are not hostile-code isolation. Use a disposable environment for model-generated source you have not reviewed.

docs.title: Run with a model
docs.text:
Install the optional SDK in the environment from setup, set OPENAI_API_KEY through your usual credential mechanism, and choose a new output directory:

python -m pip install openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
python parser.py --run ./runs/duration-parser-01
# Makes up to three model requests; provider charges may apply.
# Prints each measured score, selected source, tokens, billed spend, and final check.
# Exact scores and token counts depend on the model responses.

The declared model is gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17, overridable by OPENAI_MODEL. The official model page lists this snapshot and Responses support. Requests use a 120-second SDK timeout, zero retries, 4,096 output tokens, and reasoning effort none. The wrapper applies the SDK timeout and retry options. The SDK timeout is not a hard total wall-clock deadline across network phases.

The Responses schema provides input and output tokens, but no exact per-call bill. Total tokens are input_tokens + output_tokens; cached input is already included. Without a billed receipt, the run reports billed spend: unknown and remains usable. A monetary ceiling stops further work if a bill cannot be verified; token and trial bounds still apply. Estimates do not establish a bill, including with API-key login.

docs.title: Understand the result
docs.text:
The live command prints each measured attempt, the selected source, usage, and one separate final check. Seed is the baseline; Revision 1 is the first proposal. Best measured source is the retained winner, not necessarily the last proposal. A typed failure has no score. Development usage excludes the separate final check stored in final.json.

Live capture pending: #271 owns the retained transcript. No live improvement or score is asserted here. The seed-check comments above are measured offline output. A future live excerpt must identify its retained records and configuration; live outcomes vary.

docs.title: Keep the work
docs.text:
run_lesson(client, directory) runs the experiment through meta.run with durable storage. Choose a new directory that survives process exit. It saves:

File or directory What you can inspect later configuration.json Model declaration, attempt bound, execution limits, Python version, and implementation digest history/ Committed source versions, evaluations, evidence, feedback, decisions, and usage run-id.txt The run to reopen, including its committed prefix if accounting aborts selected.py The best measured source after a completed search final.json One separate final check, its observations, and its own usage accounting-unknown.json Accounting interruption and any available receipt, if execution aborts

With a saved run at ./runs/duration-parser-01, inspect it in a new process:

python parser.py --inspect ./runs/duration-parser-01
# Prints retained attempts, the best measured source, usage, and the final report.
# Makes no SDK requests and does not execute candidate code.

Local callables support reopening; resuming this local closure is unsupported. An accounting interruption retains committed history and available receipts, without selecting a result or running final checks. Copy a reviewed selected.py into your application to reuse it; selection does not deploy the source.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
In SEED, replace text with text.strip() in the re.fullmatch call and run --dry-run again. Predict the effect before running: the present seed's passing count stays at 17. Whitespace handling alone cannot add the missing full unit spellings or compounds in these development cases. Add a check for " 1s " to see what that change actually fixes. Changing the grader changes the experiment.

In run_lesson, change the default trials=3 to trials=1 to reduce the maximum number of rewrite requests. It need not change the selected source: the first revision may already be sufficient. Keep the final set out of both revision requests and search when adapting this lesson.

docs.title: The same loop, a different artifact
docs.text:
Role Duration parser Routing prompt Artifact / seed Python source Instructions for a response model Proposer Model writes new source Model writes new instructions Task / evaluator and objectives Python executes 40 cases; maximize passing fraction A fixed response model answers 40 tickets; Python grades labels Search Greedy, at most three revisions, stop at 1.0 Same Feedback / experience Selected parent's development observations Same, with ticket responses External limits Child execution and model request limits Request limits also apply inside evaluation

The routing lesson includes its own setup and complete source. Meta-Evolve supplies versioning, search, authorized history, selection, and accounting; your functions supply domain behavior. See the API contract for definitions.

docs.title: Complete source
Report your own cost
docs.text:
Optional custom cost reporting

The example's OpenAIClient accepts a function or bound method through cost_reporter(response). It receives the raw SDK response once and returns CostReport(usd, kind, source) or None. Save this beside the three runtime files:

run_with_cost.py · an illustrative user price, not OpenAI pricing
from decimal import Decimal
from openai_client import CostReport, OpenAIClient
from parser import run_lesson

def report_cost(response):
    usd = Decimal(response.usage.output_tokens) * Decimal("0.000002")
    return CostReport(usd, "estimated", "my output rate: USD 2 per million, v1")

with OpenAIClient.from_environment(
    cost_reporter=report_cost, cost_reporter_id="my-output-rate-v1",
) as client:
    run_lesson(client, "./runs/duration-parser-cost-01")
# An output of 1,000 tokens reports USD 0.002000 (estimated).
# Input-token cost is excluded by this chosen formula; billed spend stays unknown.

For an API lookup, replace the callback body with your own receipt client:

Callback body · billing_api is your configured client
def report_cost(response):
    receipt = billing_api.lookup(response_id=response.id)
    if receipt is None:
        return None  # Receipt unavailable: keep billed spend unknown.
    return CostReport(Decimal(receipt.usd), "billed", receipt.id)
# A receipt of USD 0.012345 reports 12,345 billed micro-USD in Usage.

CostReport is local to openai_client.py; core has no provider dependency. Use exact decimal strings and give your lookup a timeout. Change cost_reporter_id whenever pricing or lookup behavior changes. A report's kind, raw amount, rounded-up micro-USD, and source are retained as evidence. Only billed enters Usage.spend_micros; estimates remain visible in inspection. A lookup error records cost-reporting-failure and keeps the model result with unknown spend. Inspection reuses committed reports without repeating a lookup.

Empty or incomplete responses retain usage in a typed failure. Missing required token accounting after dispatch raises ExecutionAccountingUnknown; the driver saves available receipt details. A transport failure cannot become free work.

docs.title: Extract action items from meeting notes
docs.text: Status: Shipped. This case study runs offline with handwritten revisions and response fixtures. No SDK, credentials, or model requests are involved.

docs.title: The concrete problem
docs.text:
A note says “We still need someone to check the pricing.” The starting prompt, Extract action items from the meeting notes as JSON., produces an invented owner and deadline in the fixture:

[{"task": "check the pricing", "owner": "Maya", "deadline": "Friday"}]

The independent expected answer preserves the action and missing information:

[{"task": "check the pricing", "owner": null, "deadline": null}]

We improve the reusable instruction. The meeting note and expected JSON belong to the evaluator; they are not edited by the candidate.

docs.title: The complete entry point
docs.text:
main.py · complete entry point
import meta_evolve as meta

from extraction_evaluation import evaluate
from meeting_cases import DEVELOPMENT
from prompt_variants import SEED, rewrite


def rewrite_prompt(parent):
    return rewrite(parent)  # Handwritten revision; replace with your model call.


def evaluate_prompt(prompt):
    return evaluate(prompt)  # Grades fixture responses on six development cases.


result = meta.improve(
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=rewrite_prompt,
    evaluator=evaluate_prompt,
    trials=2,
)

print("Handwritten model fixtures; no live LLM calls.")
best = result.best()
print("\nPrompt          | Development cases passed")
print("----------------|-------------------------")
for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
    name = "Starting prompt" if index == 0 else f"Revision {index}"
    passed = round(attempt.metrics["score"] * len(DEVELOPMENT))
    selected = " — selected" if attempt.artifact.id == best.id else ""
    print(f"{name:<15} | {passed}/{len(DEVELOPMENT)}{selected}")
print("\nSelected prompt:")
print(best.value)
usage = result.usage()
attempt_word = "attempt" if usage.trials == 1 else "attempts"
print(f"\nUsage: {usage.trials} revision {attempt_word}, {usage.evaluations} evaluations")
Component Role here Artifact / seed The initial extraction prompt string Proposer rewrite_prompt supplies a handwritten revision Evaluator / objective evaluate_prompt checks responses against six independent JSON answers Search improve uses bounded Greedy; two revisions after seed evaluation Feedback None in this first run; explicit feedback variant below External controls Notes, expected outputs, fixture responses, attempt bound, grading

rewrite_prompt changes instructions. evaluate_prompt runs all six fixture responses and measures correctness. A later revision can regress; selection keeps the best measured prompt rather than automatically keeping the last one.

cd meta-evolve

Run the following command from the repository root. Its adjacent output is executed by the documentation evidence checks:

uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/main.py
Output
Handwritten model fixtures; no live LLM calls.

Prompt          | Development cases passed
----------------|-------------------------
Starting prompt | 2/6
Revision 1      | 5/6 — selected
Revision 2      | 3/6

Selected prompt:
Extract agreed or explicitly needed action items as a JSON array. Use task phrases from the notes with fields task, owner, deadline. Use null for unstated owners or deadlines. Exclude unaccepted suggestions.

Usage: 2 revision attempts, 3 evaluations

The seed passes 2/6 development cases, the first revision 5/6, and the second 3/6. The selected instruction adds rules for unstated fields and unaccepted suggestions. These are eighteen graded fixture responses, with no live calls.

The six development cases cover assigned work, unassigned work, missing deadlines, unaccepted suggestions, mixed notes, and no actions. The grader requires source task phrases, stated owners/deadlines, and null when missing. Row order, whitespace, and terminal sentence punctuation may differ; arbitrary paraphrases and duplicate actions fail. Expected annotations are independent of the handwritten response fixtures.

The selected prompt still omits the unassigned dashboard check in this note:

Nina will publish the release notes by Monday. We need someone to verify the dashboard. Ava suggested redesigning the homepage, but nobody agreed.

Its response keeps Nina's action and excludes Ava's suggestion, but misses:

{"task": "verify the dashboard", "owner": null, "deadline": null}

That omission explains the remaining failed case. The first command does not execute the three reserved final cases. The companion below runs them only after selection.

docs.title: Adapt and inspect
docs.text:
Replace the handwritten response/rewrite functions with your model calls, keeping case grading independent. model_integration.py provides the example-owned integration seam; a real wrapper must report usage and retain typed failures. The entire supporting source is below, including the case data and grader.

In a scratch checkout, change trials=2 to trials=1 in main.py. Predict the same 5/6 selected prompt, with one revision and two evaluations; the regressing second attempt disappears. Restore the limit afterward. Arbitrary prompt edits have no fixture responses and fail explicitly. A wrong response is a valid low score; a failed model call has a typed failure and no measurement. Fixture improvements are not measurements of a model learning or generalization to unseen meeting notes.

docs.title: Continue the same example
docs.text:
These companions keep the same prompts, meeting notes, and independent grader. Run the commands from the repository root. Every command runs offline with handwritten fixtures.

Companion Run Expected result Define better uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/define_better.py Stop at 5/6 after one revision and two evaluations. Inspect results uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/inspect_results.py Retain the 3/6 regression; compare the winner's actual and expected JSON. Change search uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/search_prompts.py Greedy reaches 6/6; BestOfN reaches 5/6 under the same attempt limit. Use feedback uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/prompt_feedback.py Development improves from 5/6 to 6/6; the selected prompt then passes 3/3 reserved cases. Inspect failed calls uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/failed_calls.py Wrong responses score zero; failed calls retain typed failures without scores. Keep a run uv run python examples/learn/meeting_notes/keep_run.py Reopen saved history, then resume a separate unfinished run from one attempt to two.

Define better. The first run uses all two allowed revisions. This companion adds a satisfaction threshold of 5 / 6 through Task and Experiment, the expanded declaration path. The first revision reaches that threshold, so search stops before trying the regression. A limit says how much work may happen; satisfaction says when the measured result is good enough to stop.

Inspect results. All measured attempts remain in result.trials(), while result.lineage() follows only the selected prompt's ancestry: seed -> improved. The command reads retained evaluation evidence to print the mixed notes, actual JSON, and expected JSON. Comparing those arrays reveals the missing verify the dashboard action without running the response fixture again.

Change search. Both runs use the same varied proposer, grader, initial prompt, and recorded random seed, with four revision attempts and five evaluations each. Greedy builds on its current best prompt; BestOfN always revises the starting prompt. The output shows each parent-to-revision step and names the comparison winner. This fixture demonstrates how parent selection changes the available revisions; it does not establish that one policy always performs better. meeting_components.py records the evaluator's configuration so comparisons keep the model, data, and grading implementation fixed.

Use feedback. Feedback is off in the first run. This companion explicitly supplies bounded, recorded ancestor evidence to the proposer. It builds a report from the latest observation of each development case and keeps only failures. After the first revision, that report contains only the mixed-notes omission. The handwritten rewriter uses it to choose the complete prompt. After selection, a separate evaluator call runs the three reserved final-check cases. Those cases never enter the search or the rewrite report; their fixture results make no generalization claim.

Inspect failed calls. A completed response containing prose instead of JSON can be graded and earns zero. An unavailable evaluator supplies no measurement, so the run has no winner; result.inspect() still exposes its failure. A failed rewrite creates no candidate artifact. The example prints these distinct outcomes instead of turning a call failure into a low score.

Keep a run. Saving a local improve() run permits read-only reopening but does not make that run resumable. The companion then creates a separate durable-local run with registered deterministic components, closes its session after one revision, closes storage, and resumes the remaining work. It checks that the complete event history equals an uninterrupted fixture run. Storage lives in a temporary directory and is deleted when the command exits.

See the SDK guide for the declaration, configuration identity, and the 20-call default bound. The three final-check calls are separate. No SDK is installed or called by import.
