docs.text: The parser quickstart uses a model to propose source; the routing quickstart also calls a model while evaluating prompts. Both use ordinary Python callables. Meta-Evolve owns the evaluated loop and history. The example owns SDK installation, credentials, requests, response decoding, and usage reporting.

docs.title: Start with the parser, then routing
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12+ on macOS or Linux. Download either the parser bundle or routing bundle into your working folder, along with the source package from this documentation build. For the parser:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip
python -m zipfile -e parser.zip .
python parser.py --dry-run
python -m pip install openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
python parser.py --run ./runs/parser-01
python parser.py --inspect ./runs/parser-01

For routing, extract prompt.zip instead and use prompt.py with a new directory. Its dry run previews cases; measuring accuracy requires model calls. Each bundle has exactly the lesson script, cases, and openai_client.py. No repository checkout or provider adapter is required. Full on-page explanations and source: parser, then routing.

docs.title: Configure and enforce requests
docs.text:
Both lessons use gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17 by default, overridden by OPENAI_MODEL. The shared wrapper enforces a 120-second SDK request timeout, no automatic retries, 4,096 output tokens, and reasoning effort none. The timeout is not a hard total wall-clock deadline. Actual declarations are saved with the experiment; changing model or wrapper configuration changes experiment identity.

The parser permits up to three rewrite requests and grades in Python. Routing permits up to 163 development requests (40 seed responses plus three rounds of one rewrite and 40 responses), then 12 separate final responses. Early stopping can reduce these counts. The candidate cannot change these controls.

Complete example-local SDK wrapper openai_client.py
"""Example-owned Responses integration with optional user-owned cost reporting."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, localcontext
from importlib.metadata import version
import os
import time
from typing import Callable, Literal

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CostReport:
    usd: Decimal
    kind: Literal["estimated", "billed"]
    source: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.usd, Decimal) or not self.usd.is_finite() or self.usd < 0:
            raise ValueError("usd must be a finite nonnegative Decimal")
        if self.kind not in ("estimated", "billed") or not isinstance(self.source, str) or not self.source.strip():
            raise ValueError("report an estimated or billed amount with its source")

    @property
    def micros(self):
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = max(28, len(self.usd.as_tuple().digits) + 6)
            return int((self.usd * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))


CostReporter = Callable[[object], CostReport | None]


def configuration():
    return {
        "model": os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL),
        "endpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1", "api": "responses",
        "timeout_seconds": 120, "max_retries": 0,
        "max_output_tokens": 4096, "reasoning_effort": "none",
        "store": False, "wrapper_revision": "2", "cost_reporter_id": None,
    }


def decode_response(response, *, elapsed, cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None):
    """Keep provider tokens, optional billed spend, and labeled cost evidence.

    Run the callback once, including for incomplete responses. A failed cost
    lookup leaves spend unknown and records its error without losing the model
    result. Missing token accounting still raises rather than fabricating zero.
    """
    evidence = []
    spend = None
    if cost_reporter is not None:
        try:
            report = cost_reporter(response)
            if report is not None:
                if not isinstance(report, CostReport):
                    raise TypeError("cost_reporter must return CostReport or None")
                evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-report", data={
                    "usd": str(report.usd), "micros": report.micros,
                    "kind": report.kind, "source": report.source,
                }))
                if report.kind == "billed":
                    spend = report.micros
        except Exception as error:
            evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-reporting-failure", data={
                "exception_type": type(error).__name__,
                "message": "Cost reporter failed; billed spend remains unknown.",
            }))
    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
    input_tokens = getattr(usage, "input_tokens", None)
    output_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", None)
    if any(type(value) is not int or value < 0 for value in (input_tokens, output_tokens)):
        error = ExecutionAccountingUnknown("Response lacks required token accounting.")
        error.receipt = {
            "response_id": getattr(response, "id", None),
            "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
            "charged_micros": spend, "wall_seconds": elapsed,
            "cost_evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in evidence],
        }
        raise error
    measured = meta.Usage(
        tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, spend_micros=spend, wall_seconds=elapsed,
    )
    text = getattr(response, "output_text", None)
    evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="openai-response", data={
        "response_id": response.id, "model": response.model,
        "status": response.status, "output_text": text,
        "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
        "charged_micros": spend,
    }))
    if response.status != "completed" or not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        return meta.ProposalResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message="model returned empty or incomplete text"),
            usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence),
        )
    return meta.ProposalResult(candidate=text, usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence))


@dataclass
class OpenAIClient:
    """The lesson knows generate() and configuration; SDK types stay here."""

    sdk: object
    configuration: dict
    cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        reporter_id = self.configuration.get("cost_reporter_id")
        if self.cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(self.cost_reporter) or not isinstance(reporter_id, str) or not reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("a callable cost reporter needs a recorded cost_reporter_id")

    @classmethod
    def from_environment(cls, *, cost_reporter=None, cost_reporter_id=None):
        if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip():
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY before requesting a live run.")
        if cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(cost_reporter) or not isinstance(cost_reporter_id, str) or not cost_reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("supply a callable cost_reporter and its cost_reporter_id")
        try:
            from openai import OpenAI
        except ImportError as error:
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Install the SDK: python -m pip install openai") from error
        settings = configuration() | {
            "sdk_version": version("openai"), "cost_reporter_id": cost_reporter_id,
        }
        sdk = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], base_url=settings["endpoint"],
                     timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"])
        return cls(sdk, settings, cost_reporter)

    def generate(self, *, instructions, input):
        settings = self.configuration
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            response = self.sdk.with_options(
                timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"],
            ).responses.create(
                model=settings["model"], instructions=instructions, input=input,
                max_output_tokens=settings["max_output_tokens"],
                reasoning={"effort": settings["reasoning_effort"]}, store=settings["store"],
            )
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown:
            raise
        except Exception as cause:
            raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown(
                "Request failed after dispatch; token accounting is unavailable."
            ) from cause
        try:
            result = decode_response(response, elapsed=0, cost_reporter=self.cost_reporter)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            error.receipt["wall_seconds"] = time.monotonic() - started
            raise
        # Include a cost lookup's elapsed time in the component's usage too.
        return replace(result, usage=replace(result.usage, wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started))

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.sdk.close()

The wrapper returns ProposalResult with text or a typed failure, known usage, and response evidence. Its generate(instructions=..., input=...) method is example-local, not a core interface. Your own SDK can use the same callable seam.

docs.title: Keep accounting and history
docs.text:
Total tokens are input plus output; cached-input tokens are already included in input. Without an exact billed receipt, spend is unknown. A monetary ceiling stops further work when spend cannot be verified; it does not reserve funds or impose a hard provider-side cap. Estimates belong in evidence.

--inspect reads saved observations without repeating requests. Reopening does not make local closures resumable, and a later model execution need not reproduce recorded answers. The parser's optional cost callback is described on its lesson page.

The extraction case study retains its distinct structured-response integration: respond(prompt, notes) and rewrite(parent, report) compose through the same boundary. Its fixtures and synthetic accounting are case-study evidence, not live performance. Source-tree edits and command grading belong to agent test-repair.

docs.title: Return a typed result
docs.text:
Use ProposalResult when the wrapper has more to report. This and the my_sdk tool example below are user-supplied SDK pseudocode:

def propose(parent, context):
    response = my_sdk.generate_structured(input=parent)
    return meta.ProposalResult(
        candidate=response.artifact,
        usage=meta.Usage(
            tokens=response.input_tokens + response.output_tokens,
            # Charged spend is shared usage; estimates stay evidence.
            spend_micros=response.charged_micros,
            wall_seconds=response.elapsed_seconds,
        ),
        metadata={"model": response.model},
        evidence=(
            meta.EvidenceDraft(
                kind="sdk-response",
                data={"estimated_cost": response.estimated_cost, "raw": response.raw},
            ),
        ),
    )

Total tokens, charged monetary spend, and elapsed time enter shared Usage. Model identity, estimated cost, granular token categories, and raw provider telemetry belong in evidence or metadata: only a figure the provider actually billed may become spend_micros. When no bill is available, explicitly report spend_micros=None. Keep input and output tokens; cached input and reasoning output are generally subsets, so use the SDK's documented totals without counting those subsets twice. A valid response remains usable. Unknown spend propagates through sums and stops further work under a monetary ceiling, as described in Money.

When a paid call fails, a wrapper has three cases, and the last is the one that is easy to miss:

  1. tokens and other required measures are known — return a typed failure carrying that usage, with unknown billed spend represented by None;
  2. the failure happened before any paid work — return a typed failure with zero usage;
  3. work may have started and required measures such as tokens are unavailable — raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown.

The names come from two submodules:

from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput          # and the other failures
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

Known spend_micros is an integer, so convert before reporting — a float raises. Round up, so the framework never under-reports a charge, and keep the raw provider figure in evidence as provenance.

Convert through Decimal, not by multiplying the float. Binary floats do not hold decimal amounts exactly, and the error goes the wrong way at exact micro boundaries: 0.000123 * 1_000_000 evaluates to 123.00000000000001, so a math.ceil of that produces 124 micro-USD for an amount that is exactly 123. Over-reporting money is a defect, not a safe direction.

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, InvalidOperation, localcontext

def charged_micros(cost_usd: object) -> int | None:
    """Exact micro-USD, rounded up, or an explicitly unknown amount."""

    try:
        # str() first: it yields the shortest decimal that round-trips the
        # value, so Decimal("0.000123") -- not the binary approximation.
        amount = cost_usd if isinstance(cost_usd, Decimal) else Decimal(str(cost_usd))
    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
    if not amount.is_finite() or amount < 0:
        return None
    with localcontext() as context:
        context.prec = max(28, len(amount.as_tuple().digits) + 6)
        return int((amount * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))

For an unreadable amount, retain a cost-reporting failure in evidence and report unknown spend. Missing token accounting still requires the case-3 escape.

Decode the amount exactly, before it becomes a float. The conversion above is only as exact as its input, and str(float) recovers just the digits the float kept — by then 0.0001230000000000000000001 is already 0.000123, and rounding up gives 123 micro-USD instead of 124. A float cannot be repaired after the fact. So read the charge from the raw body:

body = json.loads(response.text, parse_float=Decimal)
micros = charged_micros((body.get("usage") or {}).get("cost"))

If your client hands you a decoded object rather than text, take the amount from somewhere exact — a Decimal, an integer, or a decimal string — rather than a float that has already been rounded.

The duration-parser lesson supplies an optional cost_reporter(response) callback on its example-owned SDK wrapper. It accepts a function or bound method, so users can calculate a token-price estimate or call their own billing API. Its CostReport explicitly labels estimated versus billed, retains the source, and records the reporter's version in configuration. These are example types; core needs only ordinary ProposalResult/EvaluationResult, Usage, and evidence. A committed report is read back during inspection, without invoking the callback again.

Never raise an ordinary exception after billing, and never return a bare Failure: both paths reach the adapter with no usage field, so the framework records zero and the charge is lost. This is a framework guarantee about those channels, not something conformance can detect on your behalf.

Trial and evaluation counts are coordinator-owned; reporting either at the proposer boundary produces typed InvalidOutput. The meeting-notes evaluator rejects response-wrapper counts as a failed measurement, retaining known usage.

At the proposer boundary, ordinary SDK exceptions become ProposerFailure. Framework failures about durable state, accounting, or run capability escape unchanged: EventStreamConflict, DurableCorruption, InvalidSearchHistory, ExperienceStoreUnavailable, ExecutionAccountingUnknown, and CapabilityError.

docs.title: Give an SDK audited pull tools
docs.text:
When an SDK supports custom tools, register a user-owned handler that delegates to context.experience:

used = []

def search_experience(arguments):
    if context.experience is None:
        raise meta.ExperienceAccessDenied("pull access was not granted")
    observation = context.experience.search(**arguments)
    used.extend(record.ref for record in observation.records)
    return observation

response = my_sdk.run(tools={"search_experience": search_experience})
return meta.ProposalResult(
    candidate=response.artifact,
    derived_from=tuple(dict.fromkeys(used)),
)

The exact observation API is defined by ExperienceReader. The callback may run in process, or a user-owned RPC service may forward each request to this scoped handler and return its result. The RPC service must not cache or broaden the reader capability. Meta-Evolve adds no generic tool server or agent process.

Access denial, exhaustion, audit-store failure, and unknown accounting retain their normal semantics because the SDK tool calls the authoritative reader. SDKs without custom-tool support can receive pushed context.bundle data, but that is context injection rather than agent-directed pull.

The credential-free 06_user_owned_sdk example contains a complete deterministic fake SDK and audited tool callback. An acceptance-gated milestone may own an opt-in real-client experiment, as M8 does for harness validation. There is no generic provider smoke directory: a live script must serve a current gate, add no package dependency, and retain its single authorized outcome honestly.

docs.title: Authority and reproducibility
docs.text:
The wrapper may propose candidate content. It cannot choose the evaluator, change the run budget, grant itself experience, edit audit history, or promote a result. External evaluation and durable storage remain the sources of score, accounting, and lineage truth.

Committed requests, evidence, usage, failures, and artifacts support inspection and replay. Meta-Evolve does not claim that a later external SDK call will regenerate byte-identical output.

API details: ProposalResult, ProposerContext, and EvidenceDraft.

docs.title: Runs and results
docs.text:
meta.improve() is the smallest bounded local path. It evaluates the seed, asks the proposer for successors, evaluates each valid successor independently, and uses greedy search to decide where work goes next.

import meta_evolve as meta

items = ("outline", "draft", "review")

def complete_one(completed):
    return (*completed, items[len(completed)])

result = meta.improve(
    seed=(),
    proposer=complete_one,
    evaluator=len,
    trials=3,
)

That call lowers exactly to:

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(evaluator=len),
    seed=(),
    proposer=complete_one,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
)
result = meta.run(experiment)

Use the expansion for custom artifacts, objectives, satisfaction thresholds, task budgets, search, context, experience, execution mode, or registry components. Experiment owns declaration fields; storage=, mode=, and a narrowing budget= remain call-level execution overlays. The declaration-keyword run() form remains supported through 1.x and is not the taught path.

improve(storage=Storage.durable(...)) persists local history, but the façade does not claim durable-local reconstruction or resumability. Those require an explicit Experiment, registered reconstructible components, and run(..., mode="durable-local").

docs.title: Pace one decision at a time
docs.text:
Session is the execution form beneath run(). Start it when a caller needs to observe each completed policy decision:

with meta.Session.start(experiment, storage=storage) as session:
    first = session.step()
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
result = session.run

The seed is already bootstrapped when start() returns. A successful step() returns one immutable trial, archive, or stop decision only after its authorized work is complete. Manual steps and later iteration continue without repeating a decision. A newly committed stop is yielded once; repeated terminal step() calls return the same cached stop view without writes.

Leaving the context closes only that handle's execution scope. Its stable session.run and session.stopped remain queryable, and caller-owned storage stays open. Exit does not invent a stop for an incomplete run.

The seed is an evaluated baseline, not trial zero. Every successor proposal has its own trial and either an artifact plus evaluation or a typed failure.

docs.title: Search presets
docs.text:
Search changes allocation, not proposer or evaluator semantics:

  • Greedy expands the current best successful artifact.
  • BestOfN samples independent successors from the seed.
  • BestOfK samples k successors from the current incumbent, then reselects the global incumbent so later cohorts can compose. It interpolates the two presets above: k=1 reproduces Greedy's chain, and any k at or above max_trials never completes a cohort and so reproduces BestOfN's star. Because a cohort advances the frontier by at most one level, k also bounds how far a run can travel from the seed — depth <= ceil(max_trials / k). That is a ceiling, not a guarantee: the frontier only advances when a child actually beats the frozen parent.
  • Population retains a bounded population and uses deterministic tournament selection.
  • Specialists (from meta_evolve.policies import Specialists) retains the best successful occurrence for each of a configured tuple of metrics and expands a uniformly sampled metric's owner. It is GEPA-style per-key retention, not a Pareto archive, and is namespaced rather than root-exported.
  • TreeSearch (from meta_evolve.policies import TreeSearch) reconstructs a mutation tree from durable history, widens a node while child_count < ceil(sqrt(node_visits)), and otherwise descends by normalized best-descendant UCT. It is namespaced rather than root-exported.

All presets consume the same declared Budget and expose the same Run queries.

docs.title: Functional incumbent refinement
docs.text:
Use @search when a bounded custom policy only needs to choose between the seed and current incumbent:

@meta.search(max_trials=20)
def incumbent_refinement(search):
    """Expand the best measured artifact."""
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

The decorated value is an ordinary bindable search program and can be placed directly on Experiment.search. The callback receives opaque occurrence handles, immutable search.configuration, search.expand(parent), and search.stop(reason)—not SearchState, budgets, proposer references, trial records, or randomness. Additional behavior-affecting values are declared on the decorator, for example @meta.search(max_trials=20, patience=3), and are persisted in SearchSpec and included in run identity. Captured closure values are rejected with guidance to declare configuration and keep helpers at module scope.

The callback name is humanized in recorded decisions, and the first cleaned docstring line becomes its summary. Envelope stops such as objective satisfaction, the trial limit, and budget exhaustion use the same narration. Unsupported returns fail before proposer work and name the supported expand() and stop() actions.

Memory and durable storage both work in ordinary local mode. Reconstructible durable-local execution is the existing full extension workflow: register a module-level policy factory under the decorated policy reference, alongside the proposer and evaluator. The façade performs no ambient or automatic registration. Use SearchProgram.next() when a policy needs multiple parents, archive updates, populations, or other kernel decisions.

docs.title: Query the result
docs.text:
• best() decodes the selected artifact value.
  • best_trial() returns its TrialView.
  • trials() returns every seed and successor outcome in logical order.
  • inspect() returns one winner-independent RunInspection from one validated replay.
  • lineage() follows the selected artifact's causal parents.
  • summary() returns score, usage, experience use, and winning lineage.
  • compare(other) checks declaration compatibility before naming a winner.

Run is inspectable even when no successor succeeds. best() then raises the typed NoSuccessfulEvaluation rather than inventing a low score.

inspect() is the complete read boundary for authors and presentation code. Its overview separates lifecycle (complete or incomplete) from rankability (rankable or unrankable), so failed evaluations and recoverable prefixes do not become synthetic run states or scores. declaration retains the resolved search (including the default max_trials=20), component roles, budgets, capabilities, context, experience, and root random seed. Occurrence-ordered trials, typed decisions, evidence, and artifacts expose the complete history without exposing events or replay projections. The bootstrap seed is a trial at logical step zero, never a search decision.

Decision inspection is a real sum type: TrialDecisionView names selected parents and an optional completed trial, ArchiveDecisionView reports admission, eviction, and resulting membership, and StopDecisionView reports the terminal reason. Every variant carries its durable identity, logical step, non-optional rationale, and named randomness.

docs.title: Artifact values
docs.text: Plain Python values use the default codec. Text, SourceTree, and SkillSet provide shipped typed domains. Every accepted successor is frozen before commitment and records distinct occurrence identity plus parent lineage.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Comparison refuses incompatible task, evaluator, artifact, model/environment, or relevant declaration identity through RunsNotComparable. Random seed, context, and experience differences remain visible compatibility flags when the comparison contract permits them. A comparison is measured evidence, never a promotion.

docs.title: Define good enough
docs.text:
Question: when should the parser stop improving? For an exploratory run, passing 34 of 40 development checks may be enough to inspect the next idea. A stricter run can keep trying until all 40 pass. The evaluator measures correctness; a satisfaction threshold declares when to stop.

Status: Experimental/live-only. The runnable optimization uses model calls. The seed calculation below is deterministic and requires no SDK or credentials.

Component This lesson Artifact / seed Same incomplete duration parser Proposer Same source-rewriting callable and model settings Task / evaluator and objectives Change: satisfaction threshold, from 1.0 to 0.85 Search Same Greedy search, at most three revisions Feedback / experience Same selected-parent development checks External limits Same grading cases and execution limits; threshold remains outside candidate authority

docs.title: Set up this page
docs.text:
Download the threshold lesson.

Use Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Unzip this page's download into a new directory and open a terminal there. Download the matching source package into that directory too. No previous lesson or checkout is needed.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip

This installs the package from the same documentation build as the lesson. The download contains this page's script plus parser.py (grader and saved-run driver), parser_cases.py (cases), and openai_client.py (SDK boundary). Their complete source is available below.

docs.title: Change the objective declaration
docs.text:
threshold_parser.py · declaration
def declaration(client, target=0.85):
    base = experiment(client)
    task = replace(base.task, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=target),))
    return replace(base, task=task)

Maximize still prefers larger passing fractions. satisfy=0.85 lets search stop once a measured candidate reaches that fraction. It does not rescale the score, make failed measurements rankable, or require three attempts to be used.

Check the starting point in the same download:

Run in Python from the download directory
from parser import SEED, evaluate

score = evaluate(SEED).metrics["score"]
print(f"Seed: {score:.1%}")
print("Enough for 0.40:", score >= 0.40)
print("Enough for 0.85:", score >= 0.85)
# Output:
# Seed: 42.5%
# Enough for 0.40: True
# Enough for 0.85: False

The seed is measured before any rewrite. At a target of 0.40, it already suffices, so the search makes no proposal. This is successful early stopping, not an optimization gain. At 0.85, the seed is insufficient; the search can make up to three attempts to find a qualifying revision.

docs.title: Run with a different target
docs.text:
For commands marked model calls, also install openai and set OPENAI_API_KEY through your usual credential mechanism:

python -m pip install openai

The shared client uses gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17; OPENAI_MODEL overrides it. It records the actual configuration, uses a 120-second request timeout, zero automatic retries, and at most 4,096 output tokens per request. Each parser search allows at most three rewrite requests, four development evaluations including the seed, and one separate 12-case final evaluation. The final check uses Python only and never triggers another rewrite.

Provider charges may apply. Tokens include input plus output; cached input is already included. Missing billed spend remains unknown. Saved history records known usage and typed failures; a missing token receipt stops execution with retained accounting details. Exact model output and improvement vary.

The grader runs source in a fresh bounded child process without API credentials. This is trusted development execution, with a three-second wall limit, two-second CPU limit, and 65,536-byte output limit. It does not isolate hostile code from your filesystem or network; use a disposable environment for unreviewed source.

python threshold_parser.py ./runs/threshold-01 --target 0.85
# Model calls: stops on satisfaction or exhaustion and saves every attempt.
python parser.py --inspect ./runs/threshold-01
# Reads saved results without new requests.
threshold_parser.py · complete runnable script
"""Change when the parser is good enough. Makes model calls unless the seed suffices."""

import argparse
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import meta_evolve as meta
from openai_client import OpenAIClient
from parser import experiment, run_lesson


def declaration(client, target=0.85):
    base = experiment(client)
    task = replace(base.task, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=target),))
    return replace(base, task=task)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    cli.add_argument("directory", type=Path, help="new history directory")
    cli.add_argument("--target", type=float, default=0.85)
    args = cli.parse_args()
    with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
        run_lesson(client, args.directory, declaration=declaration(client, args.target))

Suppose a revision passes 34 checks. The 0.85 target stops there with unused attempts. The 1.0 target can continue; a later regression does not replace that earlier best candidate. These are conditional examples of the rules, not claims about what the model will produce.

The 12 final checks happen once after selection. They never trigger additional revisions. Passing a development threshold does not establish performance on unseen inputs or authorize deploying the parser.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text: Run with --target 0.40 in a new directory. Predict zero revisions, one development evaluation, and the unchanged seed as the winner. The CLI still initializes its configured client, so it requires SDK setup and credentials, but the satisfied seed triggers no model request. Final checks still run once. Then raise the target to 1.0: the maximum remains three attempts, and reaching a perfect score is not guaranteed.

parser_cases.py · contract
CONTRACT = """Implement parse_seconds(text: str) -> int.
1. Accept only nonnegative ASCII integer quantities (0-9).
2. Units: s/sec/secs/second/seconds, m/min/mins/minute/minutes,
   h/hr/hrs/hour/hours; return the total in seconds.
3. Accept one or more quantity-unit pairs, case-insensitive, with optional
   whitespace before, between, or after tokens; repeated units add together.
4. Raise ValueError for everything else: empty input, decimals, signs,
   colon notation, unsupported units, missing quantities/units, or junk.
"""
Reused experiment: proposer, evaluator, search, and feedback parser.py · experiment
def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.

        task=meta.Task(

Complete parser driver and grader parser.py
"""Improve source against independent checks. Trusted development, POSIX only.

Run with --dry-run to inspect the seed without an SDK or credentials.
The three-file lesson is explained in docs/learn/llm-parser.md.
"""

import argparse
from dataclasses import asdict
from hashlib import sha256
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown
from meta_evolve.domain import (
    EvaluatorFailure, InfrastructureFailure, InvalidOutput,
    ResourceExhausted, TimeoutFailure,
)

from parser_cases import CONTRACT, DEVELOPMENT

SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    """Parse a whole number of seconds or minutes."""
    import re
    match = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+)(s|m)", text)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("expected seconds or minutes")
    quantity, unit = match.groups()
    return int(quantity) * (60 if unit == "m" else 1)
'''

CHILD_SECONDS = 3
OUTPUT_BYTES = 65_536
RUNNER = '''import json, resource, sys
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (2, 2))
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (65536, 65536))
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))
scope = {}
exec(compile(open("candidate.py").read(), "candidate.py", "exec"), scope)
parse = scope.get("parse_seconds")
if not callable(parse):
    print(json.dumps({"invalid": "missing parse_seconds callable"}))
    sys.exit(0)
rows = []
for text in json.load(sys.stdin):
    try:
        value = parse(text)
        rows.append({"value": value} if type(value) is int else
                    {"error": "expected int, got " + type(value).__name__})
    except Exception as error:
        rows.append({"error": type(error).__name__})
print(json.dumps(rows))
'''


def evaluate(source, *, cases=DEVELOPMENT):
    """Run only candidate inputs in a bounded child; grade here in the parent."""
    if not cases:
        raise ValueError("evaluation requires at least one case")
    started = time.monotonic()
    evidence = ()
    failure = None
    try:
        if not isinstance(source, str) or len(source.encode()) > OUTPUT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("source must be text of at most 65536 bytes")
        compile(source, "candidate.py", "exec")  # Validate syntax without executing it.
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError, TypeError, RecursionError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)))
    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="duration-parser-") as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            (root / "candidate.py").write_text(source)
            with (root / "input.json").open("w+") as inputs, \
                    (root / "output.json").open("w+b") as output:
                json.dump([text for text, _ in cases], inputs)
                inputs.seek(0)
                process = subprocess.Popen(
                    [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", RUNNER], cwd=root,
                    env={"PATH": os.defpath, "HOME": directory, "TMPDIR": directory},
                    stdin=inputs, stdout=output, stderr=output, start_new_session=True,
                )
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=CHILD_SECONDS)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate exceeded 3 seconds")
                finally:
                    try:
                        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                    except ProcessLookupError:
                        pass
                    process.wait()
                output.seek(0)
                raw = output.read(OUTPUT_BYTES)
            evidence = (meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="parser-process", data={
                "returncode": process.returncode, "output": raw.decode(errors="replace"),
            }),)
            if failure is None:
                if len(raw) >= OUTPUT_BYTES or process.returncode == -signal.SIGXFSZ:
                    failure = ResourceExhausted(message="candidate output exceeded 65536 bytes")
                elif process.returncode in (-signal.SIGXCPU, -signal.SIGKILL):
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate hit its CPU limit")
                elif process.returncode != 0:
                    failure = EvaluatorFailure(message="candidate failed before case results")
    except OSError as error:
        failure = InfrastructureFailure(message=f"cannot execute candidate: {error}")
    usage = meta.Usage(wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started)
    if failure is not None:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=failure, evidence=evidence, usage=usage)
    try:
        rows = json.loads(raw)
        if not isinstance(rows, list) or len(rows) != len(cases):
            raise ValueError("expected one result per case and a parse_seconds callable")
        for row in rows:
            if not isinstance(row, dict) or not (
                set(row) == {"value"} and type(row["value"]) is int
                or set(row) == {"error"} and isinstance(row["error"], str)
            ):
                raise ValueError("invalid case result")
    except (ValueError, UnicodeError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)), evidence=evidence, usage=usage,
        )
    checks = tuple(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="duration-case", data={
        "input": text, "expected": expected, "actual": row,
        "passed": row == ({"error": "ValueError"} if expected is None else {"value": expected}),
    }) for (text, expected), row in zip(cases, rows))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(checks)},
        evidence=checks, usage=usage,
    )


def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )


def lesson_identity():
    """Keep local histories distinct when implementation or grading changes."""
    root = Path(__file__).parent
    return {
        "sha256": sha256(b"".join((root / name).read_bytes() for name in
                                 ("parser.py", "parser_cases.py", "openai_client.py"))).hexdigest(),
        "python": sys.version, "child_seconds": CHILD_SECONDS, "output_bytes": OUTPUT_BYTES,
    }


def show(result):
    for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
        outcome = attempt.failure.kind if attempt.failure else (
            f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.0%}" if attempt.metrics else "incomplete"
        )
        print(f"{'Seed' if index == 0 else 'Revision ' + str(index)}: {outcome}")
        for name, value in attempt.metrics.items():
            if name != "score":
                print(f"  {name}: {value:.1%}")
    try:
        print("Best measured source:\n" + result.best().value)
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        print("No successfully measured source.")
    print(f"Usage: {result.usage().trials} revisions, {result.usage().evaluations} evaluations")
    usage = result.usage()
    spend = "unknown" if usage.spend_micros is None else f"{usage.spend_micros} micro-USD"
    print(f"Tokens: {usage.tokens}; billed spend: {spend}")
    for item in result.inspect().evidence:
        if item.kind == "cost-report":
            print(f"Reported cost: USD {item.data['usd']} ({item.data['kind']}; {item.data['source']})")
        elif item.kind == "cost-reporting-failure":
            print(f"Cost report unavailable: {item.data['exception_type']}")


def run_lesson(client, directory, *, seed=SEED, trials=3, budget=None, declaration=None):
    """Save a parser experiment; a supplied declaration replaces seed/trials defaults."""
    configured = declaration if declaration is not None else experiment(client, seed=seed, trials=trials)
    root = Path(directory)
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    (root / "configuration.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity(),
        "trials": configured.search.configuration["max_trials"],
        "search": {"policy": asdict(configured.search.policy),
                   "configuration": dict(configured.search.configuration)},
        "context": None if configured.context is None else {
            "policy": asdict(configured.context.policy), **asdict(configured.context)},
        "objectives": [{"direction": type(item).__name__, **asdict(item)}
                       for item in configured.task.objectives],
        "task_budget": asdict(configured.task.budget) if configured.task.budget else None,
        "environment": dict(configured.task.environment), "random_seed": configured.random_seed,
        "budget": asdict(budget) if budget else None,
    }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
    with meta.Storage.durable(root / "history") as storage:
        try:
            result = meta.run(configured, storage=storage, budget=budget)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            (root / "accounting-unknown.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                "reason": str(error), "receipt": getattr(error, "receipt", None),
            }, indent=2) + "\n")
            raise
        finally:
            # Even an accounting escape leaves its committed prefix inspectable.
            if storage.runs():
                (root / "run-id.txt").write_text(storage.runs()[0].value + "\n")
        show(result)
        try:
            selected = result.best().value
        except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
            print("Separate final check: skipped; no successfully measured source.")
            return result.id
        (root / "selected.py").write_text(selected)
        from parser_cases import FINAL

        final = evaluate(selected, cases=FINAL)
        (root / "final.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "metrics": dict(final.metrics),
            "failure": final.failure.kind if final.failure else None,
            "evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in final.evidence],
            "usage": asdict(final.usage),
        }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
        print("Separate final check:", final.failure.kind if final.failure else
              f"{round(final.metrics['score'] * len(FINAL))}/{len(FINAL)}")
        return result.id


def main():
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    modes = cli.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    modes.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="grade only the seed; no SDK requests")
    modes.add_argument("--run", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="save a new experiment")
    modes.add_argument("--inspect", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="reopen without model calls")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    if args.dry_run:
        measured = evaluate(SEED)
        if measured.failure:
            cli.exit(1, f"{measured.failure.kind}: {measured.failure.message}\n")
        print("Dry run: no SDK requests; only the seed is evaluated.")
        print(f"Seed: {round(measured.metrics['score'] * len(DEVELOPMENT))}/{len(DEVELOPMENT)} development cases")
        for item in measured.evidence[:6]:
            row = item.data
            print(f"{row['input']!r}: {dict(row['actual'])}; expected {row['expected']}")
    elif args.inspect:
        from meta_evolve.domain import RunId

        with meta.Storage.read_only(args.inspect / "history") as storage:
            show(meta.Run(RunId((args.inspect / "run-id.txt").read_text().strip()), storage))
        final_path = args.inspect / "final.json"
        print("Separate final check:", final_path.read_text() if final_path.exists() else "not recorded")
    else:
        from openai_client import OpenAIClient

        try:
            with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
                run_lesson(client, args.run)
        except meta.CapabilityError as error:
            cli.exit(2, f"{error}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Example-owned Responses integration with optional user-owned cost reporting."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, localcontext
from importlib.metadata import version
import os
import time
from typing import Callable, Literal

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CostReport:
    usd: Decimal
    kind: Literal["estimated", "billed"]
    source: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.usd, Decimal) or not self.usd.is_finite() or self.usd < 0:
            raise ValueError("usd must be a finite nonnegative Decimal")
        if self.kind not in ("estimated", "billed") or not isinstance(self.source, str) or not self.source.strip():
            raise ValueError("report an estimated or billed amount with its source")

    @property
    def micros(self):
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = max(28, len(self.usd.as_tuple().digits) + 6)
            return int((self.usd * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))


CostReporter = Callable[[object], CostReport | None]


def configuration():
    return {
        "model": os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL),
        "endpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1", "api": "responses",
        "timeout_seconds": 120, "max_retries": 0,
        "max_output_tokens": 4096, "reasoning_effort": "none",
        "store": False, "wrapper_revision": "2", "cost_reporter_id": None,
    }


def decode_response(response, *, elapsed, cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None):
    """Keep provider tokens, optional billed spend, and labeled cost evidence.

    Run the callback once, including for incomplete responses. A failed cost
    lookup leaves spend unknown and records its error without losing the model
    result. Missing token accounting still raises rather than fabricating zero.
    """
    evidence = []
    spend = None
    if cost_reporter is not None:
        try:
            report = cost_reporter(response)
            if report is not None:
                if not isinstance(report, CostReport):
                    raise TypeError("cost_reporter must return CostReport or None")
                evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-report", data={
                    "usd": str(report.usd), "micros": report.micros,
                    "kind": report.kind, "source": report.source,
                }))
                if report.kind == "billed":
                    spend = report.micros
        except Exception as error:
            evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-reporting-failure", data={
                "exception_type": type(error).__name__,
                "message": "Cost reporter failed; billed spend remains unknown.",
            }))
    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
    input_tokens = getattr(usage, "input_tokens", None)
    output_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", None)
    if any(type(value) is not int or value < 0 for value in (input_tokens, output_tokens)):
        error = ExecutionAccountingUnknown("Response lacks required token accounting.")
        error.receipt = {
            "response_id": getattr(response, "id", None),
            "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
            "charged_micros": spend, "wall_seconds": elapsed,
            "cost_evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in evidence],
        }
        raise error
    measured = meta.Usage(
        tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, spend_micros=spend, wall_seconds=elapsed,
    )
    text = getattr(response, "output_text", None)
    evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="openai-response", data={
        "response_id": response.id, "model": response.model,
        "status": response.status, "output_text": text,
        "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
        "charged_micros": spend,
    }))
    if response.status != "completed" or not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        return meta.ProposalResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message="model returned empty or incomplete text"),
            usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence),
        )
    return meta.ProposalResult(candidate=text, usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence))


@dataclass
class OpenAIClient:
    """The lesson knows generate() and configuration; SDK types stay here."""

    sdk: object
    configuration: dict
    cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        reporter_id = self.configuration.get("cost_reporter_id")
        if self.cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(self.cost_reporter) or not isinstance(reporter_id, str) or not reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("a callable cost reporter needs a recorded cost_reporter_id")

    @classmethod
    def from_environment(cls, *, cost_reporter=None, cost_reporter_id=None):
        if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip():
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY before requesting a live run.")
        if cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(cost_reporter) or not isinstance(cost_reporter_id, str) or not cost_reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("supply a callable cost_reporter and its cost_reporter_id")
        try:
            from openai import OpenAI
        except ImportError as error:
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Install the SDK: python -m pip install openai") from error
        settings = configuration() | {
            "sdk_version": version("openai"), "cost_reporter_id": cost_reporter_id,
        }
        sdk = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], base_url=settings["endpoint"],
                     timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"])
        return cls(sdk, settings, cost_reporter)

    def generate(self, *, instructions, input):
        settings = self.configuration
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            response = self.sdk.with_options(
                timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"],
            ).responses.create(
                model=settings["model"], instructions=instructions, input=input,
                max_output_tokens=settings["max_output_tokens"],
                reasoning={"effort": settings["reasoning_effort"]}, store=settings["store"],
            )
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown:
            raise
        except Exception as cause:
            raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown(
                "Request failed after dispatch; token accounting is unavailable."
            ) from cause
        try:
            result = decode_response(response, elapsed=0, cost_reporter=self.cost_reporter)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            error.receipt["wall_seconds"] = time.monotonic() - started
            raise
        # Include a cost lookup's elapsed time in the component's usage too.
        return replace(result, usage=replace(result.usage, wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started))

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.sdk.close()

Download the search comparison.

Use Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Unzip this page's download into a new directory and open a terminal there. Download the matching source package into that directory too. No previous lesson or checkout is needed.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip

This installs the package from the same documentation build as the lesson. The download contains this page's script plus parser.py (grader and saved-run driver), parser_cases.py (cases), and openai_client.py (SDK boundary). Their complete source is available below.

docs.title: Change the search declaration
docs.text:
search_parser.py · the only experimental difference
def declarations(client, attempts=3):
    base = experiment(client, trials=attempts)
    return (
        ("greedy", base),
        ("best-of-n", replace(base, search=meta.BestOfN(max_trials=attempts))),
    )

experiment(client) assembles the parser loop. Python's dataclasses.replace creates a new immutable declaration while reusing the other components. Both runs use the same initial source, evaluator, objective, model settings, feedback selection, random seed, and declared maximum work.

Policy Parent for the next proposal What to look for Greedy Best measured source so far Later revisions can build on earlier improvements BestOfN Original seed every time Independent alternatives can explore different repairs

For example, after a successful unit-spelling repair, Greedy supplies that repaired source on the next request. BestOfN supplies the original source. The model still chooses what edit to make. Neither policy guarantees improvement.

docs.title: Run and compare
docs.text:
For commands marked model calls, also install openai and set OPENAI_API_KEY through your usual credential mechanism:

python -m pip install openai

The shared client uses gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17; OPENAI_MODEL overrides it. It records the actual configuration, uses a 120-second request timeout, zero automatic retries, and at most 4,096 output tokens per request. Each parser search allows at most three rewrite requests, four development evaluations including the seed, and one separate 12-case final evaluation. The final check uses Python only and never triggers another rewrite.

Provider charges may apply. Tokens include input plus output; cached input is already included. Missing billed spend remains unknown. Saved history records known usage and typed failures; a missing token receipt stops execution with retained accounting details. Exact model output and improvement vary.

The grader runs source in a fresh bounded child process without API credentials. This is trusted development execution, with a three-second wall limit, two-second CPU limit, and 65,536-byte output limit. It does not isolate hostile code from your filesystem or network; use a disposable environment for unreviewed source.

python search_parser.py ./runs/search-01
# Model calls: prints Search: greedy, followed by that run's results,
# then Search: best-of-n and its results. Exact scores vary.
# At most six rewrite requests in total; each run may stop early.
python parser.py --inspect ./runs/search-01/greedy
python parser.py --inspect ./runs/search-01/best-of-n
# Reopens both saved histories without new requests or candidate execution.

"""Compare parent selection with equal declared attempt limits. Makes model calls."""

import argparse
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import meta_evolve as meta
from openai_client import OpenAIClient
from parser import experiment, run_lesson


def declarations(client, attempts=3):
    base = experiment(client, trials=attempts)
    return (
        ("greedy", base),
        ("best-of-n", replace(base, search=meta.BestOfN(max_trials=attempts))),
    )


def compare(client, directory, attempts=3):
    for name, declaration in declarations(client, attempts):
        print("Search:", name)
        run_lesson(client, Path(directory) / name, declaration=declaration)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    cli.add_argument("directory", type=Path, help="new directory for both histories")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
        compare(client, args.directory)

Each directory contains its configuration, run ID, complete history, selected source, and separate final report. Compare parent source, retained scores, stop reason, and actual usage, as well as the winner. A perfect revision can stop one run before it uses all three attempts. Equal declared limits do not promise equal request counts, token use, billed spend, or final scores.

A tie keeps the earlier best occurrence. Under Greedy, a worse revision stays in history but does not become the next parent. Under BestOfN, all revisions have the seed as their parent, even if one revision beats it.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Change attempts=3 to attempts=1 in compare and use a new output directory. Each policy can now make at most one rewrite request and two development evaluations. Both first requests use the seed and its same authorized feedback. Their live answers can still differ; a fixed model declaration does not force identical provider responses.

The useful prediction is about which source is supplied, not which policy will achieve a better score. To inspect exact parent occurrences, use run.trials() and each attempt's parent_ids while the storage handle is open.

"""Improve source against independent checks. Trusted development, POSIX only.

Run with --dry-run to inspect the seed without an SDK or credentials.
The three-file lesson is explained in docs/learn/llm-parser.md.
"""

import argparse
from dataclasses import asdict
from hashlib import sha256
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown
from meta_evolve.domain import (
    EvaluatorFailure, InfrastructureFailure, InvalidOutput,
    ResourceExhausted, TimeoutFailure,
)

from parser_cases import CONTRACT, DEVELOPMENT

SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    """Parse a whole number of seconds or minutes."""
    import re
    match = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+)(s|m)", text)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("expected seconds or minutes")
    quantity, unit = match.groups()
    return int(quantity) * (60 if unit == "m" else 1)
'''

CHILD_SECONDS = 3
OUTPUT_BYTES = 65_536
RUNNER = '''import json, resource, sys
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (2, 2))
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (65536, 65536))
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))
scope = {}
exec(compile(open("candidate.py").read(), "candidate.py", "exec"), scope)
parse = scope.get("parse_seconds")
if not callable(parse):
    print(json.dumps({"invalid": "missing parse_seconds callable"}))
    sys.exit(0)
rows = []
for text in json.load(sys.stdin):
    try:
        value = parse(text)
        rows.append({"value": value} if type(value) is int else
                    {"error": "expected int, got " + type(value).__name__})
    except Exception as error:
        rows.append({"error": type(error).__name__})
print(json.dumps(rows))
'''


def evaluate(source, *, cases=DEVELOPMENT):
    """Run only candidate inputs in a bounded child; grade here in the parent."""
    if not cases:
        raise ValueError("evaluation requires at least one case")
    started = time.monotonic()
    evidence = ()
    failure = None
    try:
        if not isinstance(source, str) or len(source.encode()) > OUTPUT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("source must be text of at most 65536 bytes")
        compile(source, "candidate.py", "exec")  # Validate syntax without executing it.
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError, TypeError, RecursionError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)))
    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="duration-parser-") as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            (root / "candidate.py").write_text(source)
            with (root / "input.json").open("w+") as inputs, \
                    (root / "output.json").open("w+b") as output:
                json.dump([text for text, _ in cases], inputs)
                inputs.seek(0)
                process = subprocess.Popen(
                    [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", RUNNER], cwd=root,
                    env={"PATH": os.defpath, "HOME": directory, "TMPDIR": directory},
                    stdin=inputs, stdout=output, stderr=output, start_new_session=True,
                )
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=CHILD_SECONDS)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate exceeded 3 seconds")
                finally:
                    try:
                        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                    except ProcessLookupError:
                        pass
                    process.wait()
                output.seek(0)
                raw = output.read(OUTPUT_BYTES)
            evidence = (meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="parser-process", data={
                "returncode": process.returncode, "output": raw.decode(errors="replace"),
            }),)
            if failure is None:
                if len(raw) >= OUTPUT_BYTES or process.returncode == -signal.SIGXFSZ:
                    failure = ResourceExhausted(message="candidate output exceeded 65536 bytes")
                elif process.returncode in (-signal.SIGXCPU, -signal.SIGKILL):
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate hit its CPU limit")
                elif process.returncode != 0:
                    failure = EvaluatorFailure(message="candidate failed before case results")
    except OSError as error:
        failure = InfrastructureFailure(message=f"cannot execute candidate: {error}")
    usage = meta.Usage(wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started)
    if failure is not None:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=failure, evidence=evidence, usage=usage)
    try:
        rows = json.loads(raw)
        if not isinstance(rows, list) or len(rows) != len(cases):
            raise ValueError("expected one result per case and a parse_seconds callable")
        for row in rows:
            if not isinstance(row, dict) or not (
                set(row) == {"value"} and type(row["value"]) is int
                or set(row) == {"error"} and isinstance(row["error"], str)
            ):
                raise ValueError("invalid case result")
    except (ValueError, UnicodeError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)), evidence=evidence, usage=usage,
        )
    checks = tuple(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="duration-case", data={
        "input": text, "expected": expected, "actual": row,
        "passed": row == ({"error": "ValueError"} if expected is None else {"value": expected}),
    }) for (text, expected), row in zip(cases, rows))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(checks)},
        evidence=checks, usage=usage,
    )


def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )


def lesson_identity():
    """Keep local histories distinct when implementation or grading changes."""
    root = Path(__file__).parent
    return {
        "sha256": sha256(b"".join((root / name).read_bytes() for name in
                                 ("parser.py", "parser_cases.py", "openai_client.py"))).hexdigest(),
        "python": sys.version, "child_seconds": CHILD_SECONDS, "output_bytes": OUTPUT_BYTES,
    }


def show(result):
    for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
        outcome = attempt.failure.kind if attempt.failure else (
            f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.0%}" if attempt.metrics else "incomplete"
        )
        print(f"{'Seed' if index == 0 else 'Revision ' + str(index)}: {outcome}")
        for name, value in attempt.metrics.items():
            if name != "score":
                print(f"  {name}: {value:.1%}")
    try:
        print("Best measured source:\n" + result.best().value)
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        print("No successfully measured source.")
    print(f"Usage: {result.usage().trials} revisions, {result.usage().evaluations} evaluations")
    usage = result.usage()
    spend = "unknown" if usage.spend_micros is None else f"{usage.spend_micros} micro-USD"
    print(f"Tokens: {usage.tokens}; billed spend: {spend}")
    for item in result.inspect().evidence:
        if item.kind == "cost-report":
            print(f"Reported cost: USD {item.data['usd']} ({item.data['kind']}; {item.data['source']})")
        elif item.kind == "cost-reporting-failure":
            print(f"Cost report unavailable: {item.data['exception_type']}")


def run_lesson(client, directory, *, seed=SEED, trials=3, budget=None, declaration=None):
    """Save a parser experiment; a supplied declaration replaces seed/trials defaults."""
    configured = declaration if declaration is not None else experiment(client, seed=seed, trials=trials)
    root = Path(directory)
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    (root / "configuration.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity(),
        "trials": configured.search.configuration["max_trials"],
        "search": {"policy": asdict(configured.search.policy),
                   "configuration": dict(configured.search.configuration)},
        "context": None if configured.context is None else {
            "policy": asdict(configured.context.policy), **asdict(configured.context)},
        "objectives": [{"direction": type(item).__name__, **asdict(item)}
                       for item in configured.task.objectives],
        "task_budget": asdict(configured.task.budget) if configured.task.budget else None,
        "environment": dict(configured.task.environment), "random_seed": configured.random_seed,
        "budget": asdict(budget) if budget else None,
    }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
    with meta.Storage.durable(root / "history") as storage:
        try:
            result = meta.run(configured, storage=storage, budget=budget)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            (root / "accounting-unknown.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                "reason": str(error), "receipt": getattr(error, "receipt", None),
            }, indent=2) + "\n")
            raise
        finally:
            # Even an accounting escape leaves its committed prefix inspectable.
            if storage.runs():
                (root / "run-id.txt").write_text(storage.runs()[0].value + "\n")
        show(result)
        try:
            selected = result.best().value
        except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
            print("Separate final check: skipped; no successfully measured source.")
            return result.id
        (root / "selected.py").write_text(selected)
        from parser_cases import FINAL

        final = evaluate(selected, cases=FINAL)
        (root / "final.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "metrics": dict(final.metrics),
            "failure": final.failure.kind if final.failure else None,
            "evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in final.evidence],
            "usage": asdict(final.usage),
        }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
        print("Separate final check:", final.failure.kind if final.failure else
              f"{round(final.metrics['score'] * len(FINAL))}/{len(FINAL)}")
        return result.id


def main():
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    modes = cli.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    modes.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="grade only the seed; no SDK requests")
    modes.add_argument("--run", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="save a new experiment")
    modes.add_argument("--inspect", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="reopen without model calls")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    if args.dry_run:
        measured = evaluate(SEED)
        if measured.failure:
            cli.exit(1, f"{measured.failure.kind}: {measured.failure.message}\n")
        print("Dry run: no SDK requests; only the seed is evaluated.")
        print(f"Seed: {round(measured.metrics['score'] * len(DEVELOPMENT))}/{len(DEVELOPMENT)} development cases")
        for item in measured.evidence[:6]:
            row = item.data
            print(f"{row['input']!r}: {dict(row['actual'])}; expected {row['expected']}")
    elif args.inspect:
        from meta_evolve.domain import RunId

        with meta.Storage.read_only(args.inspect / "history") as storage:
            show(meta.Run(RunId((args.inspect / "run-id.txt").read_text().strip()), storage))
        final_path = args.inspect / "final.json"
        print("Separate final check:", final_path.read_text() if final_path.exists() else "not recorded")
    else:
        from openai_client import OpenAIClient

        try:
            with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
                run_lesson(client, args.run)
        except meta.CapabilityError as error:
            cli.exit(2, f"{error}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
