"""Example-owned Responses integration with optional user-owned cost reporting."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, localcontext
from importlib.metadata import version
import os
import time
from typing import Callable, Literal

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CostReport:
    usd: Decimal
    kind: Literal["estimated", "billed"]
    source: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.usd, Decimal) or not self.usd.is_finite() or self.usd < 0:
            raise ValueError("usd must be a finite nonnegative Decimal")
        if self.kind not in ("estimated", "billed") or not isinstance(self.source, str) or not self.source.strip():
            raise ValueError("report an estimated or billed amount with its source")

    @property
    def micros(self):
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = max(28, len(self.usd.as_tuple().digits) + 6)
            return int((self.usd * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))


CostReporter = Callable[[object], CostReport | None]


def configuration():
    return {
        "model": os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL),
        "endpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1", "api": "responses",
        "timeout_seconds": 120, "max_retries": 0,
        "max_output_tokens": 4096, "reasoning_effort": "none",
        "store": False, "wrapper_revision": "2", "cost_reporter_id": None,
    }


def decode_response(response, *, elapsed, cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None):
    """Keep provider tokens, optional billed spend, and labeled cost evidence.

    Run the callback once, including for incomplete responses. A failed cost
    lookup leaves spend unknown and records its error without losing the model
    result. Missing token accounting still raises rather than fabricating zero.
    """
    evidence = []
    spend = None
    if cost_reporter is not None:
        try:
            report = cost_reporter(response)
            if report is not None:
                if not isinstance(report, CostReport):
                    raise TypeError("cost_reporter must return CostReport or None")
                evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-report", data={
                    "usd": str(report.usd), "micros": report.micros,
                    "kind": report.kind, "source": report.source,
                }))
                if report.kind == "billed":
                    spend = report.micros
        except Exception as error:
            evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-reporting-failure", data={
                "exception_type": type(error).__name__,
                "message": "Cost reporter failed; billed spend remains unknown.",
            }))
    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
    input_tokens = getattr(usage, "input_tokens", None)
    output_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", None)
    if any(type(value) is not int or value < 0 for value in (input_tokens, output_tokens)):
        error = ExecutionAccountingUnknown("Response lacks required token accounting.")
        error.receipt = {
            "response_id": getattr(response, "id", None),
            "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
            "charged_micros": spend, "wall_seconds": elapsed,
            "cost_evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in evidence],
        }
        raise error
    measured = meta.Usage(
        tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, spend_micros=spend, wall_seconds=elapsed,
    )
    text = getattr(response, "output_text", None)
    evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="openai-response", data={
        "response_id": response.id, "model": response.model,
        "status": response.status, "output_text": text,
        "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
        "charged_micros": spend,
    }))
    if response.status != "completed" or not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        return meta.ProposalResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message="model returned empty or incomplete text"),
            usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence),
        )
    return meta.ProposalResult(candidate=text, usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence))


@dataclass
class OpenAIClient:
    """The lesson knows generate() and configuration; SDK types stay here."""

    sdk: object
    configuration: dict
    cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        reporter_id = self.configuration.get("cost_reporter_id")
        if self.cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(self.cost_reporter) or not isinstance(reporter_id, str) or not reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("a callable cost reporter needs a recorded cost_reporter_id")

    @classmethod
    def from_environment(cls, *, cost_reporter=None, cost_reporter_id=None):
        if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip():
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY before requesting a live run.")
        if cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(cost_reporter) or not isinstance(cost_reporter_id, str) or not cost_reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("supply a callable cost_reporter and its cost_reporter_id")
        try:
            from openai import OpenAI
        except ImportError as error:
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Install the SDK: python -m pip install openai") from error
        settings = configuration() | {
            "sdk_version": version("openai"), "cost_reporter_id": cost_reporter_id,
        }
        sdk = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], base_url=settings["endpoint"],
                     timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"])
        return cls(sdk, settings, cost_reporter)

    def generate(self, *, instructions, input):
        settings = self.configuration
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            response = self.sdk.with_options(
                timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"],
            ).responses.create(
                model=settings["model"], instructions=instructions, input=input,
                max_output_tokens=settings["max_output_tokens"],
                reasoning={"effort": settings["reasoning_effort"]}, store=settings["store"],
            )
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown:
            raise
        except Exception as cause:
            raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown(
                "Request failed after dispatch; token accounting is unavailable."
            ) from cause
        try:
            result = decode_response(response, elapsed=0, cost_reporter=self.cost_reporter)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            error.receipt["wall_seconds"] = time.monotonic() - started
            raise
        # Include a cost lookup's elapsed time in the component's usage too.
        return replace(result, usage=replace(result.usage, wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started))

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.sdk.close()

def inspect(result):
    for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
        score = f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.1%}" if attempt.metrics else "no score"
        failure = attempt.failure.kind if attempt.failure else "none"
        print(f"Attempt {index}: {score}; failure: {failure}")
    print("Rankability:", result.inspect().overview.rankability)
    print("Revisions / evaluations:", result.usage().trials, result.usage().evaluations)
    try:
        selected = result.best()
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        print("No measured candidate to select")
        return
    print("Selected attempt:", result.trials().index(result.best_trial()))
    print("Selected source:\n" + selected.value.rstrip())
    print("Winning lineage:", len(result.lineage()))
    missed = next((item.data for item in result.best_trial().evidence
                   if item.kind == "duration-case" and not item.data["passed"]), None)
    if missed is not None:
        print(f"Missed: {missed['input']!r} -> {dict(missed['actual'])}; expected {missed['expected']}")

best().value returns selected source; best_trial() returns its measurement and evidence. The selected attempt number identifies the winning occurrence, including when later source bytes tie it. trials() includes the seed and all attempted revisions. lineage() follows the selected artifact's parents, so rejected siblings can remain in history without belonging to that lineage. inspect() and usage() work even when no attempt has a valid score.

docs.title: Distinguish a mistake from a failed measurement
docs.text:
python inspect_parser.py --invalid-seed
# Output:
# Attempt 0: no score; failure: invalid_output
# Rankability: unrankable
# Revisions / evaluations: 0 1
# No measured candidate to select

Here the script deliberately supplies invalid Python syntax. The evaluator cannot measure a parser, so it records a typed failure without a score. A failed proposal may have no artifact at all. Check attempt.failure and attempt.artifact before reading an unsuccessful revision's source.

Observation Meaning Valid source returns the wrong answer Measured failed case; lowers the score Syntax error or malformed output invalid_output; no score Child exceeds its execution limit timeout; no score A revision ties or regresses Retained in history; the earlier best remains selected Nothing was successfully evaluated Inspection still works; best() raises NoSuccessfulEvaluation

docs.title: Inspect a model-produced history
docs.text:
To create a history from this download, run the shared parser driver:

For commands marked model calls, also install openai and set OPENAI_API_KEY through your usual credential mechanism:

python -m pip install openai

The shared client uses gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17; OPENAI_MODEL overrides it. It records the actual configuration, uses a 120-second request timeout, zero automatic retries, and at most 4,096 output tokens per request. Each parser search allows at most three rewrite requests, four development evaluations including the seed, and one separate 12-case final evaluation. The final check uses Python only and never triggers another rewrite.

Provider charges may apply. Tokens include input plus output; cached input is already included. Missing billed spend remains unknown. Saved history records known usage and typed failures; a missing token receipt stops execution with retained accounting details. Exact model output and improvement vary.

The grader runs source in a fresh bounded child process without API credentials. This is trusted development execution, with a three-second wall limit, two-second CPU limit, and 65,536-byte output limit. It does not isolate hostile code from your filesystem or network; use a disposable environment for unreviewed source.

python parser.py --run ./runs/inspection-01
# Model calls: prints measured attempts, selected source, usage, and final checks.
python inspect_parser.py ./runs/inspection-01
# Reads those same attempts and the selected source; makes no model calls.

A live run may succeed immediately, tie, regress, or fail. If its scores were 42.5%, 85%, then 42.5%, the second candidate would stay selected. This is an illustration of selection, not a captured model transcript.

def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )

def evaluate(source, *, cases=DEVELOPMENT):
    """Run only candidate inputs in a bounded child; grade here in the parent."""
    if not cases:
        raise ValueError("evaluation requires at least one case")
    started = time.monotonic()
    evidence = ()
    failure = None
    try:
        if not isinstance(source, str) or len(source.encode()) > OUTPUT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("source must be text of at most 65536 bytes")
        compile(source, "candidate.py", "exec")  # Validate syntax without executing it.
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError, TypeError, RecursionError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)))
    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="duration-parser-") as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            (root / "candidate.py").write_text(source)
            with (root / "input.json").open("w+") as inputs, \
                    (root / "output.json").open("w+b") as output:
                json.dump([text for text, _ in cases], inputs)
                inputs.seek(0)
                process = subprocess.Popen(
                    [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", RUNNER], cwd=root,
                    env={"PATH": os.defpath, "HOME": directory, "TMPDIR": directory},
                    stdin=inputs, stdout=output, stderr=output, start_new_session=True,
                )
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=CHILD_SECONDS)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate exceeded 3 seconds")
                finally:
                    try:
                        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                    except ProcessLookupError:
                        pass
                    process.wait()
                output.seek(0)
                raw = output.read(OUTPUT_BYTES)
            evidence = (meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="parser-process", data={
                "returncode": process.returncode, "output": raw.decode(errors="replace"),
            }),)
            if failure is None:
                if len(raw) >= OUTPUT_BYTES or process.returncode == -signal.SIGXFSZ:
                    failure = ResourceExhausted(message="candidate output exceeded 65536 bytes")
                elif process.returncode in (-signal.SIGXCPU, -signal.SIGKILL):
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate hit its CPU limit")
                elif process.returncode != 0:
                    failure = EvaluatorFailure(message="candidate failed before case results")
    except OSError as error:
        failure = InfrastructureFailure(message=f"cannot execute candidate: {error}")
    usage = meta.Usage(wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started)
    if failure is not None:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=failure, evidence=evidence, usage=usage)
    try:
        rows = json.loads(raw)
        if not isinstance(rows, list) or len(rows) != len(cases):
            raise ValueError("expected one result per case and a parse_seconds callable")
        for row in rows:
            if not isinstance(row, dict) or not (
                set(row) == {"value"} and type(row["value"]) is int
                or set(row) == {"error"} and isinstance(row["error"], str)
            ):
                raise ValueError("invalid case result")
    except (ValueError, UnicodeError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)), evidence=evidence, usage=usage,
        )
    checks = tuple(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="duration-case", data={
        "input": text, "expected": expected, "actual": row,
        "passed": row == ({"error": "ValueError"} if expected is None else {"value": expected}),
    }) for (text, expected), row in zip(cases, rows))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(checks)},
        evidence=checks, usage=usage,
    )


def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )


def lesson_identity():
    """Keep local histories distinct when implementation or grading changes."""
    root = Path(__file__).parent
    return {
        "sha256": sha256(b"".join((root / name).read_bytes() for name in
                                 ("parser.py", "parser_cases.py", "openai_client.py"))).hexdigest(),
        "python": sys.version, "child_seconds": CHILD_SECONDS, "output_bytes": OUTPUT_BYTES,
    }


def show(result):
    for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
        outcome = attempt.failure.kind if attempt.failure else (
            f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.0%}" if attempt.metrics else "incomplete"
        )
        print(f"{'Seed' if index == 0 else 'Revision ' + str(index)}: {outcome}")
        for name, value in attempt.metrics.items():
            if name != "score":
                print(f"  {name}: {value:.1%}")
    try:
        print("Best measured source:\n" + result.best().value)
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        print("No successfully measured source.")
    print(f"Usage: {result.usage().trials} revisions, {result.usage().evaluations} evaluations")
    usage = result.usage()
    spend = "unknown" if usage.spend_micros is None else f"{usage.spend_micros} micro-USD"
    print(f"Tokens: {usage.tokens}; billed spend: {spend}")
    for item in result.inspect().evidence:
        if item.kind == "cost-report":
            print(f"Reported cost: USD {item.data['usd']} ({item.data['kind']}; {item.data['source']})")
        elif item.kind == "cost-reporting-failure":
            print(f"Cost report unavailable: {item.data['exception_type']}")


def run_lesson(client, directory, *, seed=SEED, trials=3, budget=None, declaration=None):
    """Save a parser experiment; a supplied declaration replaces seed/trials defaults."""
    configured = declaration if declaration is not None else experiment(client, seed=seed, trials=trials)
    root = Path(directory)
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    (root / "configuration.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity(),
        "trials": configured.search.configuration["max_trials"],
        "search": {"policy": asdict(configured.search.policy),
                   "configuration": dict(configured.search.configuration)},
        "context": None if configured.context is None else {
            "policy": asdict(configured.context.policy), **asdict(configured.context)},
        "objectives": [{"direction": type(item).__name__, **asdict(item)}
                       for item in configured.task.objectives],
        "task_budget": asdict(configured.task.budget) if configured.task.budget else None,
        "environment": dict(configured.task.environment), "random_seed": configured.random_seed,
        "budget": asdict(budget) if budget else None,
    }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
    with meta.Storage.durable(root / "history") as storage:
        try:
            result = meta.run(configured, storage=storage, budget=budget)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            (root / "accounting-unknown.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                "reason": str(error), "receipt": getattr(error, "receipt", None),
            }, indent=2) + "\n")
            raise
        finally:
            # Even an accounting escape leaves its committed prefix inspectable.
            if storage.runs():
                (root / "run-id.txt").write_text(storage.runs()[0].value + "\n")
        show(result)
        try:
            selected = result.best().value
        except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
            print("Separate final check: skipped; no successfully measured source.")
            return result.id
        (root / "selected.py").write_text(selected)
        from parser_cases import FINAL

        final = evaluate(selected, cases=FINAL)
        (root / "final.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "metrics": dict(final.metrics),
            "failure": final.failure.kind if final.failure else None,
            "evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in final.evidence],
            "usage": asdict(final.usage),
        }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
        print("Separate final check:", final.failure.kind if final.failure else
              f"{round(final.metrics['score'] * len(FINAL))}/{len(FINAL)}")
        return result.id


def main():
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    modes = cli.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    modes.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="grade only the seed; no SDK requests")
    modes.add_argument("--run", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="save a new experiment")
    modes.add_argument("--inspect", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="reopen without model calls")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    if args.dry_run:
        measured = evaluate(SEED)
        if measured.failure:
            cli.exit(1, f"{measured.failure.kind}: {measured.failure.message}\n")
        print("Dry run: no SDK requests; only the seed is evaluated.")
        print(f"Seed: {round(measured.metrics['score'] * len(DEVELOPMENT))}/{len(DEVELOPMENT)} development cases")
        for item in measured.evidence[:6]:
            row = item.data
            print(f"{row['input']!r}: {dict(row['actual'])}; expected {row['expected']}")
    elif args.inspect:
        from meta_evolve.domain import RunId

        with meta.Storage.read_only(args.inspect / "history") as storage:
            show(meta.Run(RunId((args.inspect / "run-id.txt").read_text().strip()), storage))
        final_path = args.inspect / "final.json"
        print("Separate final check:", final_path.read_text() if final_path.exists() else "not recorded")
    else:
        from openai_client import OpenAIClient

        try:
            with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
                run_lesson(client, args.run)
        except meta.CapabilityError as error:
            cli.exit(2, f"{error}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Complete SDK boundary and accounting openai_client.py
"""Example-owned Responses integration with optional user-owned cost reporting."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, localcontext
from importlib.metadata import version
import os
import time
from typing import Callable, Literal

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CostReport:
    usd: Decimal
    kind: Literal["estimated", "billed"]
    source: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.usd, Decimal) or not self.usd.is_finite() or self.usd < 0:
            raise ValueError("usd must be a finite nonnegative Decimal")
        if self.kind not in ("estimated", "billed") or not isinstance(self.source, str) or not self.source.strip():
            raise ValueError("report an estimated or billed amount with its source")

    @property
    def micros(self):
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = max(28, len(self.usd.as_tuple().digits) + 6)
            return int((self.usd * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))


CostReporter = Callable[[object], CostReport | None]


def configuration():
    return {
        "model": os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL),
        "endpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1", "api": "responses",
        "timeout_seconds": 120, "max_retries": 0,
        "max_output_tokens": 4096, "reasoning_effort": "none",
        "store": False, "wrapper_revision": "2", "cost_reporter_id": None,
    }


def decode_response(response, *, elapsed, cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None):
    """Keep provider tokens, optional billed spend, and labeled cost evidence.

    Run the callback once, including for incomplete responses. A failed cost
    lookup leaves spend unknown and records its error without losing the model
    result. Missing token accounting still raises rather than fabricating zero.
    """
    evidence = []
    spend = None
    if cost_reporter is not None:
        try:
            report = cost_reporter(response)
            if report is not None:
                if not isinstance(report, CostReport):
                    raise TypeError("cost_reporter must return CostReport or None")
                evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-report", data={
                    "usd": str(report.usd), "micros": report.micros,
                    "kind": report.kind, "source": report.source,
                }))
                if report.kind == "billed":
                    spend = report.micros
        except Exception as error:
            evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-reporting-failure", data={
                "exception_type": type(error).__name__,
                "message": "Cost reporter failed; billed spend remains unknown.",
            }))
    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
    input_tokens = getattr(usage, "input_tokens", None)
    output_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", None)
    if any(type(value) is not int or value < 0 for value in (input_tokens, output_tokens)):
        error = ExecutionAccountingUnknown("Response lacks required token accounting.")
        error.receipt = {
            "response_id": getattr(response, "id", None),
            "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
            "charged_micros": spend, "wall_seconds": elapsed,
            "cost_evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in evidence],
        }
        raise error
    measured = meta.Usage(
        tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, spend_micros=spend, wall_seconds=elapsed,
    )
    text = getattr(response, "output_text", None)
    evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="openai-response", data={
        "response_id": response.id, "model": response.model,
        "status": response.status, "output_text": text,
        "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
        "charged_micros": spend,
    }))
    if response.status != "completed" or not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        return meta.ProposalResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message="model returned empty or incomplete text"),
            usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence),
        )
    return meta.ProposalResult(candidate=text, usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence))


@dataclass
class OpenAIClient:
    """The lesson knows generate() and configuration; SDK types stay here."""

    sdk: object
    configuration: dict
    cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        reporter_id = self.configuration.get("cost_reporter_id")
        if self.cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(self.cost_reporter) or not isinstance(reporter_id, str) or not reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("a callable cost reporter needs a recorded cost_reporter_id")

    @classmethod
    def from_environment(cls, *, cost_reporter=None, cost_reporter_id=None):
        if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip():
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY before requesting a live run.")
        if cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(cost_reporter) or not isinstance(cost_reporter_id, str) or not cost_reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("supply a callable cost_reporter and its cost_reporter_id")
        try:
            from openai import OpenAI
        except ImportError as error:
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Install the SDK: python -m pip install openai") from error
        settings = configuration() | {
            "sdk_version": version("openai"), "cost_reporter_id": cost_reporter_id,
        }
        sdk = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], base_url=settings["endpoint"],
                     timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"])
        return cls(sdk, settings, cost_reporter)

    def generate(self, *, instructions, input):
        settings = self.configuration
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            response = self.sdk.with_options(
                timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"],
            ).responses.create(
                model=settings["model"], instructions=instructions, input=input,
                max_output_tokens=settings["max_output_tokens"],
                reasoning={"effort": settings["reasoning_effort"]}, store=settings["store"],
            )
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown:
            raise
        except Exception as cause:
            raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown(
                "Request failed after dispatch; token accounting is unavailable."
            ) from cause
        try:
            result = decode_response(response, elapsed=0, cost_reporter=self.cost_reporter)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            error.receipt["wall_seconds"] = time.monotonic() - started
            raise
        # Include a cost lookup's elapsed time in the component's usage too.
        return replace(result, usage=replace(result.usage, wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started))

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.sdk.close()

docs.text:
Status: Shipped. Both examples on this page use handwritten repairs and real subprocess graders, with no model calls or credentials.

A source file can be the candidate too. This complete example repairs a small clamp() function against three independent checks. Copy it into a Python file with meta_evolve installed; the candidate and grader are both inline.

docs.title: Propose a patch and measure it
docs.text:
SourceTree stores immutable source. PatchProposer applies a TextPatch in a private mutable workspace and captures an immutable successor. The patch names one file, its exact expected bytes, and the replacement. CommandEvaluator independently materializes each candidate and runs the evaluator-owned grader.

The fixed repair is handwritten. The example demonstrates the API and evaluation boundary, not a model discovering a repair.

import sys
import meta_evolve as meta

BAD = "def clamp(value, low, high):\n    return value\n"
FIXED = "def clamp(value, low, high):\n    return max(low, min(value, high))\n"
seed = meta.SourceTree({"clamp.py": BAD})


def repair(tree, context):
    return meta.TextPatch(path="clamp.py", expected=tree["clamp.py"], replacement=FIXED)


# The grader belongs to the evaluator, outside the candidate's source tree.
GRADER = """
import runpy
try:
    clamp = runpy.run_path("clamp.py")["clamp"]
    passed = all(clamp(value, 0, 10) == expected
                 for value, expected in ((-5, 0), (5, 5), (15, 10)))
except Exception:
    passed = False
raise SystemExit(0 if passed else 1)
"""
evaluator = meta.CommandEvaluator(
    command=meta.ProcessSpec(argv=(sys.executable, "-c", GRADER)),
    environment=meta.EvaluationEnvironment(name="clamp-checks", version="1"),
)
result = meta.run(meta.Experiment(
    seed=seed,
    task=meta.Task(artifact=meta.SourceTree, evaluator=evaluator),
    proposer=meta.PatchProposer(repair),
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=1),
))
print("Scores:", [t.metrics["score"] for t in result.trials()])
print("Parent unchanged:", seed["clamp.py"] == BAD)
print("Selected source:")
print(result.best().value["clamp.py"], end="")
print("Usage:", result.usage().trials, result.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# Scores: [0.0, 1.0]
# Parent unchanged: True
# Selected source:
# def clamp(value, low, high):
#     return max(low, min(value, high))
# Usage: 1 2

The grader checks all three inputs. Exit 0 passes the suite; exit 1 is a valid failing measurement. The poor candidate remains a measured result with score 0.0. Candidate load or execution errors also fail this particular grader's suite.

The evaluator records process evidence alongside each measurement. trials() retains both candidates, and lineage() follows the selected source's parents. A patch whose expected bytes do not match produces InvalidOutput; an evaluator infrastructure failure produces EvaluatorFailure. Neither becomes a low score.

The proposer edits source, not the grader, budget, or promotion rules. The local subprocess is a development execution boundary, not a sandbox for hostile code. These three selection checks are not an untouched final test split, and passing them establishes nothing about other functions.

docs.text: A booking tool should merge touching ranges: (9, 10) and (10, 11) must become (9, 11). The maintained agent_test_repair application starts with source that merges overlaps but leaves touching bookings separate. Its fixture replaces start < merged[-1][1] with start <= merged[-1][1].

Use Python 3.12+ on macOS or Linux with subprocess execution, Git, and uv:

cd meta-evolve
uv sync --locked

Run from the repository root. These first output lines are checked against the actual command; it also prints the selected source and evaluations: 2.

docs.title: The actual declaration
docs.text:
This function comes from the maintained application:

main.py · repair_intervals
def repair_intervals(
    build_agent: Callable[[str], Proposer],
    *,
    grader: Path = GRADER,
    random_seed: int = 0,
) -> meta.Run:
    """Run the repair loop with one agent factory and one grader.

    Both are injectable so the same loop serves every caller: ``main`` passes
    the committed fixture, a live run passes a factory that wraps a real model
    SDK, and the test suite passes counting fixtures and a deliberately broken
    grader. Nothing else about the task, seed, search, or budget changes.
    """

    experiment = meta.Experiment(
        task=grading_task(grader),
        seed=meta.load_source_tree(CANDIDATE),
        proposer=build_agent(INSTRUCTIONS),
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=MAX_TRIALS),
        random_seed=random_seed,
    )
    return meta.run(experiment)

CANDIDATE names the directory containing only intervals.py. INSTRUCTIONS describes the failing case; build_agent returns a source-tree proposer. The fixture already knows the fix. grading_task owns the external runner, grader, score threshold of 1.0, and budget of at most two revisions and three evaluations. Greedy stops after the first passing revision. No context policy is configured. The candidate cannot edit the grader or expand these limits.

The independent grader covers overlapping, disjoint, touching, contained, and unsorted ranges. Its runner interprets exit 0 as score 1.0, exit 1 as score 0.0, and a missing/crashing grader as EvaluatorFailure with no score. A candidate that cannot import fails its tests; it is distinct from a broken grader.

These cases guide selection and are not an untouched final split. The local process boundary is not hostile-code isolation. Passing tests here demonstrates this repair, not model ability or correctness for an arbitrary repository.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
In a scratch checkout, make the replacement string in fixture_agent identical to its original start < merged[-1][1]. Rerun: predict scores: [0.0], grader passed: False, and evaluations: 3. Both allowed revisions are tried, but the printed scores follow only the selected artifact's lineage: the seed remains selected because neither revision improves it. All three evaluations remain in result.trials(). Restore the fixture afterward.

For your own task, replace the candidate files, instruction brief, and independent grader. Supply an SDK-backed callable factory to repair_intervals to replace the fixture; keep evaluation and permissions outside candidate authority.

docs.title: Complete booking-range source
docs.text:
candidate/intervals.py 
"""Collapse booking ranges into the blocks an operator actually sees.

A range is an inclusive ``(start, end)`` pair. Two ranges belong to the same
block when they overlap *or* touch: ``(9, 10)`` and ``(10, 11)`` describe one
uninterrupted block from 9 to 11 and must come back as ``(9, 11)``.
"""


def merge_intervals(intervals):
    """Return the fewest non-touching blocks covering ``intervals``, in order."""

    merged = []
    for start, end in sorted(intervals):
        if merged and start < merged[-1][1]:
            last_start, last_end = merged[-1]
            merged[-1] = (last_start, max(last_end, end))
        else:
            merged.append((start, end))
    return merged
grader.py 
"""Evaluator-owned checks for the materialized interval candidate."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import traceback
from pathlib import Path


# Overlapping and disjoint ranges are the cases anyone writes first, and the
# shipped code gets both right. Only the touching ones — where a block ends
# exactly where the next begins — catch the defect.
CASES: tuple[tuple[list[tuple[int, int]], list[tuple[int, int]]], ...] = (
    ([], []),
    ([(1, 4)], [(1, 4)]),
    ([(1, 3), (2, 4)], [(1, 4)]),
    ([(1, 5), (2, 3)], [(1, 5)]),
    ([(1, 2), (4, 5)], [(1, 2), (4, 5)]),
    ([(5, 6), (1, 2)], [(1, 2), (5, 6)]),
    ([(1, 2), (2, 3)], [(1, 3)]),
    ([(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (6, 7)], [(1, 4), (6, 7)]),
)


def _mismatch(merge, intervals, expected) -> str | None:
    actual = merge(list(intervals))
    # The block type is the candidate's call; the block contents are not.
    if [tuple(block) for block in actual] == expected:
        return None
    return f"merge_intervals({intervals!r}) returned {actual!r}, expected {expected!r}"


def grade(workspace: Path) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Anything the candidate causes — wrong answers, code that fails to
    load or run — is an ordinary failure. Only a grader-internal fault may
    escape as an exception, which the runner reports outside the pass/fail
    protocol.
    """

    try:
        candidate = workspace / "intervals.py"
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("candidate_intervals", candidate)
        if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
            raise ImportError(f"cannot load candidate module: {candidate}")
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
        merge = module.merge_intervals
        failures = [
            message
            for intervals, expected in CASES
            if (message := _mismatch(merge, intervals, expected)) is not None
        ]
    except Exception:
        return False, f"candidate failed to load or run:\n{traceback.format_exc()}"
    if failures:
        return False, "\n".join(failures)
    return True, f"all {len(CASES)} merge_intervals cases passed"
main.py 
"""An injected proposer repairs a real bug; a grader subprocess decides.

The seed is a ``SourceTree`` holding a function whose documented contract and
shipped behaviour disagree on one character. The proposer is supplied by the
caller through the user-owned callable boundary: the committed script injects
a deterministic fixture, and a real SDK wrapper plugs into the same seam. The
evaluator is a *separate process* running an evaluator-owned grader the
proposer never sees, so the score is a verdict about the code rather than a
report from the thing being scored.

The grader obeys the fixed exit protocol: ``0`` passes, ``1`` is a rankable
failure with a failing score, and anything else is an ``EvaluatorFailure``.
That third code is the load-bearing one here. With an agent in the loop, a
grader that is itself broken must not quietly rank every attempt as bad work;
it must stop the run and say so.

Every piece is importable and injectable: ``repair_intervals`` takes the agent
factory and the grader path, so a deterministic test drives this same logic
through counting fixture proposers and a deliberately broken grader.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.ports import Proposer


HERE = Path(__file__).parent
CANDIDATE = HERE / "candidate"
RUNNER = HERE / "run_grader.py"
GRADER = HERE / "grader.py"

AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120.0
# One proposal per trial, and the run stops early the moment the grader
# passes. The wall ceiling is sized for a live SDK wrapper whose sessions each
# stay inside AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, plus the grader subprocesses between
# them; the committed fixture never comes near it.
MAX_TRIALS = 2
BUDGET = meta.Budget(
    evaluations=MAX_TRIALS + 1,
    trials=MAX_TRIALS,
    wall_seconds=AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * (MAX_TRIALS + 1),
)

# What a developer is handed by CI: the failing case, not the fix. The repo
# states the contract in the module docstring; finding the one character that
# disagrees with it is the agent's job.
INSTRUCTIONS = (
    "The test suite for intervals.py fails one case: "
    "merge_intervals([(1, 2), (2, 3)]) returned [(1, 2), (2, 3)] where "
    "[(1, 3)] was expected. Read intervals.py, find why it disagrees with "
    "the contract it documents, and fix it. Change only intervals.py, and "
    "keep merge_intervals' name and signature."
)


def grading_task(grader: Path = GRADER) -> meta.Task:
    """Score candidates by running the grader in its own process.

    ``CommandEvaluator`` materializes each candidate tree into a fresh
    workspace and runs the fixed runner there. The grader lives outside
    ``candidate/``, so it is never part of any ``SourceTree`` a proposal
    could read or edit, and its exit code — not anything the candidate
    prints about itself — is what becomes the score.
    """

    return meta.Task(
        evaluator=meta.CommandEvaluator(
            command=meta.ProcessSpec(
                argv=(sys.executable, str(RUNNER), str(grader)),
                environment={"PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"},
            ),
            environment=meta.EvaluationEnvironment(
                name="python-intervals-tests",
                version="1",
            ),
        ),
        artifact=meta.SourceTree,
        # Stop as soon as the grader passes: further attempts cost money and
        # cannot improve on a passing suite.
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
        budget=BUDGET,
    )


def repair_intervals(
    build_agent: Callable[[str], Proposer],
    *,
    grader: Path = GRADER,
    random_seed: int = 0,
) -> meta.Run:
    """Run the repair loop with one agent factory and one grader.

    Both are injectable so the same loop serves every caller: ``main`` passes
    the committed fixture, a live run passes a factory that wraps a real model
    SDK, and the test suite passes counting fixtures and a deliberately broken
    grader. Nothing else about the task, seed, search, or budget changes.
    """

    experiment = meta.Experiment(
        task=grading_task(grader),
        seed=meta.load_source_tree(CANDIDATE),
        proposer=build_agent(INSTRUCTIONS),
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=MAX_TRIALS),
        random_seed=random_seed,
    )
    return meta.run(experiment)


def fixture_agent(_instructions: str) -> Proposer:
    """The committed proposer: a deterministic stand-in for an SDK wrapper.

    It occupies exactly the seat a user-owned SDK wrapper occupies — a factory
    that takes the instructions and returns an ordinary proposer callable —
    but it already knows the one-character repair, so the committed script
    runs offline, credential-free, and for free. It takes no shortcut past the
    evaluator: its candidate is scored by the same grader subprocess a live
    wrapper's would be, and the instructions it ignores are the ones a live
    wrapper would forward to its model.
    """

    def repair(tree: meta.SourceTree, _context) -> meta.SourceTree:
        return meta.SourceTree(
            {
                **tree,
                "intervals.py": tree["intervals.py"].replace(
                    "start < merged[-1][1]", "start <= merged[-1][1]"
                ),
            }
        )

    return repair


def main() -> None:
    """Run the loop with the fixture and print what the grader decided.

    Swap ``fixture_agent`` for your own factory to put a real agent in the
    loop; the printing below distinguishes "the best candidate scored X" from
    "nothing was scored at all", which is the difference the exit protocol
    exists to preserve.
    """

    result = repair_intervals(fixture_agent)
    try:
        trial = result.best_trial()
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        # Not "every candidate is bad": no candidate was scored at all. Every
        # evaluation recorded a typed failure carrying no metric, so there is
        # nothing to rank -- a grader fault (exit 2) is the one this example
        # exists to show.
        print("no candidate scored: every evaluation failed before producing one")
        print(f"run {result.id.value} recorded why; the seed source is unchanged")
        raise SystemExit(1)
    print(f"scores: {[step.metrics['score'] for step in result.lineage()]}")
    print(f"grader passed: {trial.metrics['score'] == 1.0}")
    print(f"best source:\n{result.best().value['intervals.py']}")
    print(f"evaluations: {result.summary().evaluation_count}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
run_grader.py 
"""Fixed grader runner: exit 0 pass, 1 rankable failure, other grader fault.

The runner loads the evaluator-owned grader named by ``argv[1]`` and grades
the current working directory — the materialized candidate workspace.
Anything the candidate causes is an ordinary exit ``1``; a missing, crashing,
or malformed grader exits ``2`` so it surfaces as an ``EvaluatorFailure``
instead of ranking every candidate as failing.
"""

import importlib.util
import sys
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

exit_code = 2
try:
    grader_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("external_grader", grader_path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise ImportError(f"cannot load external grader: {grader_path}")
    grader = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(grader)
    result = grader.grade(Path.cwd())
    if (
        not isinstance(result, tuple)
        or len(result) != 2
        or type(result[0]) is not bool
        or not isinstance(result[1], str)
    ):
        raise TypeError("grader must return tuple[bool, str]")
    print(result[1])
    exit_code = 0 if result[0] else 1
except BaseException:
    traceback.print_exc()
raise SystemExit(exit_code)

docs.text:
Question: can the proposer see why the current parser failed? Suppose a revision handles "2sec" but still rejects "1h30m". The source is the candidate; the observed failed check is feedback that may help a proposer choose its next edit. Recording it does not automatically supply it to the next request.

Status: Experimental/live-only. This comparison uses model calls. Tests verify what enters each request, including after a rejected regression.

Component This lesson Artifact / seed Same parser source in both runs Proposer Same function, complete contract, and model configuration Task / evaluator and objectives Same independent development checks and perfect-score target Search Greedy, at most three revisions in each run Feedback / experience Change: omitted context versus explicit ancestor observations External limits Same cases, random seed, limits, and independent grading; separate stores

docs.title: Set up this page
docs.text:
Download the feedback comparison.

Use Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Unzip this page's download into a new directory and open a terminal there. Download the matching source package into that directory too. No previous lesson or checkout is needed.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip

This installs the package from the same documentation build as the lesson. The download contains this page's script plus parser.py (grader and saved-run driver), parser_cases.py (cases), and openai_client.py (SDK boundary). Their complete source is available below.

feedback_parser.py · comparison declarations
def declarations(client, attempts=3):

context=None supplies no prior observations. The base experiment explicitly uses AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000). That policy selects bounded committed ancestor records. The same proposer then extracts the newest duration-case observations, belonging to its selected parent.

def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )

The data flow is: evaluate source → commit case evidence → select authorized records → construct the next request. The evaluator never updates a mutable feedback dictionary shared with the proposer. The final 12 cases enter neither selection nor feedback.

Request input Feedback omitted Feedback supplied Current parent source Present Present Complete parser contract Present Present development_checks Empty list Selected parent's committed observations

A rejected revision does not replace the Greedy parent. Its case observations therefore do not replace that parent's feedback on the next request.

docs.title: Run and inspect
docs.text:
For commands marked model calls, also install openai and set OPENAI_API_KEY through your usual credential mechanism:

python -m pip install openai

The shared client uses gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17; OPENAI_MODEL overrides it. It records the actual configuration, uses a 120-second request timeout, zero automatic retries, and at most 4,096 output tokens per request. Each parser search allows at most three rewrite requests, four development evaluations including the seed, and one separate 12-case final evaluation. The final check uses Python only and never triggers another rewrite.

Provider charges may apply. Tokens include input plus output; cached input is already included. Missing billed spend remains unknown. Saved history records known usage and typed failures; a missing token receipt stops execution with retained accounting details. Exact model output and improvement vary.

The grader runs source in a fresh bounded child process without API credentials. This is trusted development execution, with a three-second wall limit, two-second CPU limit, and 65,536-byte output limit. It does not isolate hostile code from your filesystem or network; use a disposable environment for unreviewed source.

python feedback_parser.py ./runs/feedback-01
# Model calls: prints Feedback: without-feedback and Feedback: with-feedback,
# each followed by measured attempts, selected source, usage, and final checks.
# At most six rewrite requests across the two runs; scores vary.
python parser.py --inspect ./runs/feedback-01/without-feedback
python parser.py --inspect ./runs/feedback-01/with-feedback
# Reads both histories without model calls.

"""Compare omitted and explicit ancestor feedback. Makes model calls."""

import argparse
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

from openai_client import OpenAIClient
from parser import experiment, run_lesson


def declarations(client, attempts=3):
    base = experiment(client, trials=attempts)
    return (
        ("without-feedback", replace(base, context=None)),
        ("with-feedback", base),
    )


def compare(client, directory, attempts=3):
    for name, declaration in declarations(client, attempts):
        print("Feedback:", name)
        run_lesson(client, Path(directory) / name, declaration=declaration)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    cli.add_argument("directory", type=Path, help="new directory for both histories")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
        compare(client, args.directory)

Feedback changes the information available to a proposer. It does not guarantee that the model uses it well, or that this run beats the one without feedback. Both histories keep failures and known usage even when their scores differ.

Change context=None to context=base.context in declarations, rename the first label to with-feedback-again, and use a new output directory. Both conditions now explicitly supply ancestor feedback. Their request inputs follow the same rule; their model responses need not match.

For a saved run, ask: did the next request use the last proposed source or the best measured source? A regression is the case that separates those answers.

docs.text: Improving a prompt, skill document, or playbook changes the artifact. Supplying prior observations changes feedback. You can evolve a playbook without giving its proposer prior observations, or supply observations while evolving parser source. The two choices are independent.

Complete parser driver and grader parser.py
"""Improve source against independent checks. Trusted development, POSIX only.

Run with --dry-run to inspect the seed without an SDK or credentials.
The three-file lesson is explained in docs/learn/llm-parser.md.
"""

import argparse
from dataclasses import asdict
from hashlib import sha256
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown
from meta_evolve.domain import (
    EvaluatorFailure, InfrastructureFailure, InvalidOutput,
    ResourceExhausted, TimeoutFailure,
)

from parser_cases import CONTRACT, DEVELOPMENT

SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    """Parse a whole number of seconds or minutes."""
    import re
    match = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+)(s|m)", text)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("expected seconds or minutes")
    quantity, unit = match.groups()
    return int(quantity) * (60 if unit == "m" else 1)
'''

CHILD_SECONDS = 3
OUTPUT_BYTES = 65_536
RUNNER = '''import json, resource, sys
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (2, 2))
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (65536, 65536))
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))
scope = {}
exec(compile(open("candidate.py").read(), "candidate.py", "exec"), scope)
parse = scope.get("parse_seconds")
if not callable(parse):
    print(json.dumps({"invalid": "missing parse_seconds callable"}))
    sys.exit(0)
rows = []
for text in json.load(sys.stdin):
    try:
        value = parse(text)
        rows.append({"value": value} if type(value) is int else
                    {"error": "expected int, got " + type(value).__name__})
    except Exception as error:
        rows.append({"error": type(error).__name__})
print(json.dumps(rows))
'''


def evaluate(source, *, cases=DEVELOPMENT):
    """Run only candidate inputs in a bounded child; grade here in the parent."""
    if not cases:
        raise ValueError("evaluation requires at least one case")
    started = time.monotonic()
    evidence = ()
    failure = None
    try:
        if not isinstance(source, str) or len(source.encode()) > OUTPUT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("source must be text of at most 65536 bytes")
        compile(source, "candidate.py", "exec")  # Validate syntax without executing it.
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError, TypeError, RecursionError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)))
    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="duration-parser-") as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            (root / "candidate.py").write_text(source)
            with (root / "input.json").open("w+") as inputs, \
                    (root / "output.json").open("w+b") as output:
                json.dump([text for text, _ in cases], inputs)
                inputs.seek(0)
                process = subprocess.Popen(
                    [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", RUNNER], cwd=root,
                    env={"PATH": os.defpath, "HOME": directory, "TMPDIR": directory},
                    stdin=inputs, stdout=output, stderr=output, start_new_session=True,
                )
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=CHILD_SECONDS)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate exceeded 3 seconds")
                finally:
                    try:
                        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                    except ProcessLookupError:
                        pass
                    process.wait()
                output.seek(0)
                raw = output.read(OUTPUT_BYTES)
            evidence = (meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="parser-process", data={
                "returncode": process.returncode, "output": raw.decode(errors="replace"),
            }),)
            if failure is None:
                if len(raw) >= OUTPUT_BYTES or process.returncode == -signal.SIGXFSZ:
                    failure = ResourceExhausted(message="candidate output exceeded 65536 bytes")
                elif process.returncode in (-signal.SIGXCPU, -signal.SIGKILL):
                    failure = TimeoutFailure(message="candidate hit its CPU limit")
                elif process.returncode != 0:
                    failure = EvaluatorFailure(message="candidate failed before case results")
    except OSError as error:
        failure = InfrastructureFailure(message=f"cannot execute candidate: {error}")
    usage = meta.Usage(wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started)
    if failure is not None:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=failure, evidence=evidence, usage=usage)
    try:
        rows = json.loads(raw)
        if not isinstance(rows, list) or len(rows) != len(cases):
            raise ValueError("expected one result per case and a parse_seconds callable")
        for row in rows:
            if not isinstance(row, dict) or not (
                set(row) == {"value"} and type(row["value"]) is int
                or set(row) == {"error"} and isinstance(row["error"], str)
            ):
                raise ValueError("invalid case result")
    except (ValueError, UnicodeError) as error:
        return meta.EvaluationResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message=str(error)), evidence=evidence, usage=usage,
        )
    checks = tuple(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="duration-case", data={
        "input": text, "expected": expected, "actual": row,
        "passed": row == ({"error": "ValueError"} if expected is None else {"value": expected}),
    }) for (text, expected), row in zip(cases, rows))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(checks)},
        evidence=checks, usage=usage,
    )


def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )


def lesson_identity():
    """Keep local histories distinct when implementation or grading changes."""
    root = Path(__file__).parent
    return {
        "sha256": sha256(b"".join((root / name).read_bytes() for name in
                                 ("parser.py", "parser_cases.py", "openai_client.py"))).hexdigest(),
        "python": sys.version, "child_seconds": CHILD_SECONDS, "output_bytes": OUTPUT_BYTES,
    }


def show(result):
    for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
        outcome = attempt.failure.kind if attempt.failure else (
            f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.0%}" if attempt.metrics else "incomplete"
        )
        print(f"{'Seed' if index == 0 else 'Revision ' + str(index)}: {outcome}")
        for name, value in attempt.metrics.items():
            if name != "score":
                print(f"  {name}: {value:.1%}")
    try:
        print("Best measured source:\n" + result.best().value)
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        print("No successfully measured source.")
    print(f"Usage: {result.usage().trials} revisions, {result.usage().evaluations} evaluations")
    usage = result.usage()
    spend = "unknown" if usage.spend_micros is None else f"{usage.spend_micros} micro-USD"
    print(f"Tokens: {usage.tokens}; billed spend: {spend}")
    for item in result.inspect().evidence:
        if item.kind == "cost-report":
            print(f"Reported cost: USD {item.data['usd']} ({item.data['kind']}; {item.data['source']})")
        elif item.kind == "cost-reporting-failure":
            print(f"Cost report unavailable: {item.data['exception_type']}")


def run_lesson(client, directory, *, seed=SEED, trials=3, budget=None, declaration=None):
    """Save a parser experiment; a supplied declaration replaces seed/trials defaults."""
    configured = declaration if declaration is not None else experiment(client, seed=seed, trials=trials)
    root = Path(directory)
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    (root / "configuration.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity(),
        "trials": configured.search.configuration["max_trials"],
        "search": {"policy": asdict(configured.search.policy),
                   "configuration": dict(configured.search.configuration)},
        "context": None if configured.context is None else {
            "policy": asdict(configured.context.policy), **asdict(configured.context)},
        "objectives": [{"direction": type(item).__name__, **asdict(item)}
                       for item in configured.task.objectives],
        "task_budget": asdict(configured.task.budget) if configured.task.budget else None,
        "environment": dict(configured.task.environment), "random_seed": configured.random_seed,
        "budget": asdict(budget) if budget else None,
    }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
    with meta.Storage.durable(root / "history") as storage:
        try:
            result = meta.run(configured, storage=storage, budget=budget)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            (root / "accounting-unknown.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                "reason": str(error), "receipt": getattr(error, "receipt", None),
            }, indent=2) + "\n")
            raise
        finally:
            # Even an accounting escape leaves its committed prefix inspectable.
            if storage.runs():
                (root / "run-id.txt").write_text(storage.runs()[0].value + "\n")
        show(result)
        try:
            selected = result.best().value
        except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
            print("Separate final check: skipped; no successfully measured source.")
            return result.id
        (root / "selected.py").write_text(selected)
        from parser_cases import FINAL

        final = evaluate(selected, cases=FINAL)
        (root / "final.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "metrics": dict(final.metrics),
            "failure": final.failure.kind if final.failure else None,
            "evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in final.evidence],
            "usage": asdict(final.usage),
        }, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n")
        print("Separate final check:", final.failure.kind if final.failure else
              f"{round(final.metrics['score'] * len(FINAL))}/{len(FINAL)}")
        return result.id


def main():
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    modes = cli.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    modes.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="grade only the seed; no SDK requests")
    modes.add_argument("--run", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="save a new experiment")
    modes.add_argument("--inspect", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="reopen without model calls")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    if args.dry_run:
        measured = evaluate(SEED)
        if measured.failure:
            cli.exit(1, f"{measured.failure.kind}: {measured.failure.message}\n")
        print("Dry run: no SDK requests; only the seed is evaluated.")
        print(f"Seed: {round(measured.metrics['score'] * len(DEVELOPMENT))}/{len(DEVELOPMENT)} development cases")
        for item in measured.evidence[:6]:
            row = item.data
            print(f"{row['input']!r}: {dict(row['actual'])}; expected {row['expected']}")
    elif args.inspect:
        from meta_evolve.domain import RunId

        with meta.Storage.read_only(args.inspect / "history") as storage:
            show(meta.Run(RunId((args.inspect / "run-id.txt").read_text().strip()), storage))
        final_path = args.inspect / "final.json"
        print("Separate final check:", final_path.read_text() if final_path.exists() else "not recorded")
    else:
        from openai_client import OpenAIClient

        try:
            with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
                run_lesson(client, args.run)
        except meta.CapabilityError as error:
            cli.exit(2, f"{error}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Example-owned Responses integration with optional user-owned cost reporting."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, localcontext
from importlib.metadata import version
import os
import time
from typing import Callable, Literal

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CostReport:
    usd: Decimal
    kind: Literal["estimated", "billed"]
    source: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.usd, Decimal) or not self.usd.is_finite() or self.usd < 0:
            raise ValueError("usd must be a finite nonnegative Decimal")
        if self.kind not in ("estimated", "billed") or not isinstance(self.source, str) or not self.source.strip():
            raise ValueError("report an estimated or billed amount with its source")

    @property
    def micros(self):
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = max(28, len(self.usd.as_tuple().digits) + 6)
            return int((self.usd * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))


CostReporter = Callable[[object], CostReport | None]


def configuration():
    return {
        "model": os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL),
        "endpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1", "api": "responses",
        "timeout_seconds": 120, "max_retries": 0,
        "max_output_tokens": 4096, "reasoning_effort": "none",
        "store": False, "wrapper_revision": "2", "cost_reporter_id": None,
    }


def decode_response(response, *, elapsed, cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None):
    """Keep provider tokens, optional billed spend, and labeled cost evidence.

    Run the callback once, including for incomplete responses. A failed cost
    lookup leaves spend unknown and records its error without losing the model
    result. Missing token accounting still raises rather than fabricating zero.
    """
    evidence = []
    spend = None
    if cost_reporter is not None:
        try:
            report = cost_reporter(response)
            if report is not None:
                if not isinstance(report, CostReport):
                    raise TypeError("cost_reporter must return CostReport or None")
                evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-report", data={
                    "usd": str(report.usd), "micros": report.micros,
                    "kind": report.kind, "source": report.source,
                }))
                if report.kind == "billed":
                    spend = report.micros
        except Exception as error:
            evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="cost-reporting-failure", data={
                "exception_type": type(error).__name__,
                "message": "Cost reporter failed; billed spend remains unknown.",
            }))
    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
    input_tokens = getattr(usage, "input_tokens", None)
    output_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", None)
    if any(type(value) is not int or value < 0 for value in (input_tokens, output_tokens)):
        error = ExecutionAccountingUnknown("Response lacks required token accounting.")
        error.receipt = {
            "response_id": getattr(response, "id", None),
            "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
            "charged_micros": spend, "wall_seconds": elapsed,
            "cost_evidence": [dict(item.data) for item in evidence],
        }
        raise error
    measured = meta.Usage(
        tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, spend_micros=spend, wall_seconds=elapsed,
    )
    text = getattr(response, "output_text", None)
    evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="openai-response", data={
        "response_id": response.id, "model": response.model,
        "status": response.status, "output_text": text,
        "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
        "charged_micros": spend,
    }))
    if response.status != "completed" or not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        return meta.ProposalResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message="model returned empty or incomplete text"),
            usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence),
        )
    return meta.ProposalResult(candidate=text, usage=measured, evidence=tuple(evidence))


@dataclass
class OpenAIClient:
    """The lesson knows generate() and configuration; SDK types stay here."""

    sdk: object
    configuration: dict
    cost_reporter: CostReporter | None = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        reporter_id = self.configuration.get("cost_reporter_id")
        if self.cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(self.cost_reporter) or not isinstance(reporter_id, str) or not reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("a callable cost reporter needs a recorded cost_reporter_id")

    @classmethod
    def from_environment(cls, *, cost_reporter=None, cost_reporter_id=None):
        if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip():
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY before requesting a live run.")
        if cost_reporter is not None and (
            not callable(cost_reporter) or not isinstance(cost_reporter_id, str) or not cost_reporter_id.strip()
        ):
            raise ValueError("supply a callable cost_reporter and its cost_reporter_id")
        try:
            from openai import OpenAI
        except ImportError as error:
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Install the SDK: python -m pip install openai") from error
        settings = configuration() | {
            "sdk_version": version("openai"), "cost_reporter_id": cost_reporter_id,
        }
        sdk = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], base_url=settings["endpoint"],
                     timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"])
        return cls(sdk, settings, cost_reporter)

    def generate(self, *, instructions, input):
        settings = self.configuration
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            response = self.sdk.with_options(
                timeout=settings["timeout_seconds"], max_retries=settings["max_retries"],
            ).responses.create(
                model=settings["model"], instructions=instructions, input=input,
                max_output_tokens=settings["max_output_tokens"],
                reasoning={"effort": settings["reasoning_effort"]}, store=settings["store"],
            )
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown:
            raise
        except Exception as cause:
            raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown(
                "Request failed after dispatch; token accounting is unavailable."
            ) from cause
        try:
            result = decode_response(response, elapsed=0, cost_reporter=self.cost_reporter)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            error.receipt["wall_seconds"] = time.monotonic() - started
            raise
        # Include a cost lookup's elapsed time in the component's usage too.
        return replace(result, usage=replace(result.usage, wall_seconds=time.monotonic() - started))

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.sdk.close()

docs.title: Save and reuse
docs.text:
Question: how do I keep the parser and understand it after the process exits? Saving source preserves an implementation. Saving its run also preserves the attempts, measurements, failures, feedback, and lineage that explain selection. You need the history directory and its run ID to reopen that record.

Status: Shipped. Saving and reopening the seed below requires no model. The optional model-produced history uses the Experimental/live-only quickstart.

Component This lesson Artifact / seed Same parser source, exported as selected.py Proposer Unused in the seed-only rehearsal; unchanged for model runs Task / evaluator and objectives Same independent parser checks Search Zero revisions in the free rehearsal; original search retained when reopening Feedback / experience Recorded observations persist; reopening supplies no new feedback External limits Change: persistent storage and read-only reopening in a fresh process

docs.title: Set up this page
docs.text:
Download the persistence lesson.

Use Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Unzip this page's download into a new directory and open a terminal there. Download the matching source package into that directory too. No previous lesson or checkout is needed.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip

This installs the package from the same documentation build as the lesson. The download contains this page's script plus parser.py (grader and saved-run driver), parser_cases.py (cases), and openai_client.py (SDK boundary). Their complete source is available below.

docs.title: Save a seed run, then exit
docs.text:
python reuse_parser.py ./runs/saved_seed_01 --save-seed
# Output:
# Saved seed: 0 revisions, 1 evaluation

This script creates a persistent directory, not a temporary store. The process exits after writing the run ID and selected source:

reuse_parser.py · save

    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
